what-this-is/para1.en:
A site selling unique paintings — six in the catalogue at the time of writing,
priced \$60–\$440 — run by one non-technical person resident in mainland China,
addressed equally to international and domestic buyers.
what-this-is/para1.zh: 一个出售独一无二画作的网站——撰写本文时作品目录中有六幅，定价\$60–\$440——由一位居住在中国大陆、不懂技术的人经营，同等面向国际买家和国内买家。

what-this-is/para2.en:
That last sentence contains most of the difficulty. A gallery site for a
handful of works is an afternoon's work. A gallery site for a handful of works
that takes money across the Chinese border, ships physical objects
internationally, satisfies two consumer-law regimes at once and loads
acceptably on both sides of the Great Firewall is not.
what-this-is/para2.zh: 难点大多就在上面这句话里。为寥寥几件作品做一个画廊网站，一个下午就能完成。而这样一个画廊网站若要跨越中国边境收款、向海外寄送实物、同时满足两套消费者法律制度，并在防火长城内外都能以可接受的速度加载，就不是一个下午的事了。

what-this-is/para3.en:
Nothing in the build is fixed to six. The counts, the series and the page set
are all derived from the work data; adding a seventh work, or a new series, is
a data edit.
what-this-is/para3.zh: 构建中没有任何地方把数量固定为六。各项数量、系列和页面集合都由作品数据推导而来；新增第七件作品或一个新系列，只需修改数据。

sec-blockers/head.en: The seven findings that would have sunk it
sec-blockers/head.zh: 本会让网站失败的七项发现

sec-blockers/tblcap1.en: Blocking findings, all now dealt with in the build
sec-blockers/tblcap1.zh: 阻断性发现，现已全部在构建中解决

sec-blockers/cell3.en: Every call to action was `#A19E97` — **2.67:1**, failing both the body-text and the large-text floor. No font size rescues it.
sec-blockers/cell3.zh: 所有行动号召都是`#A19E97`——**2.67:1**，正文和大字号两条下限都未达到。任何字号都救不了它。

sec-blockers/cell5.en: **Stripe**\index{Stripe} is unavailable to a mainland-China seller — the whole account, not merely PayPal. **Airwallex**\index{Airwallex} excludes mainland entities from card acquiring and opens no individual accounts at all.
sec-blockers/cell5.zh: **Stripe**\index{Stripe}不向中国大陆卖家开放——整个账户都不行，而不仅仅是PayPal。**Airwallex**\index{Airwallex}在银行卡收单上排除中国大陆实体，而且根本不开设个人账户。

sec-blockers/cell7.en: `vercel.app` and `workers.dev` measure **100% blocked** from mainland China. `pages.dev` measures 0%.
sec-blockers/cell7.zh: `vercel.app`和`workers.dev`在中国大陆实测**100% 被屏蔽**。`pages.dev`实测为 0%。

sec-blockers/cell9.en: A unique pre-existing painting gets **no returns exception** under either Chinese or EU law. Uniqueness is not personalisation.
sec-blockers/cell9.zh: 一幅独一无二的现成画作，无论依中国法律还是欧盟法律，都**不享有退货例外**。独一无二不等于个性化定制。

sec-blockers/cell11.en: Instagram was the only contact channel. It is blocked in mainland China, and EU law requires an email address regardless.
sec-blockers/cell11.zh: Instagram 曾是唯一的联系渠道。它在中国大陆被屏蔽，而且无论如何，欧盟法律都要求提供电子邮件地址。

sec-blockers/cell13.en: **China-origin paintings are not duty-free into the United States.** Section 301\index{Section 301} adds 7.5% and the \$800 de minimis\index{de minimis} exemption is suspended.
sec-blockers/cell13.zh: **中国原产的画作进入美国并非免关税。**301 条款\index{Section 301}加征 7.5%，且\$800最低限度免税额\index{de minimis}豁免已被暂停。

sec-blockers/cell15.en: A one-page site cannot link to one painting, which is the site's main acquisition motion.
sec-blockers/cell15.zh: 单页网站无法链接到某一幅画，而这正是网站获取买家的主要方式。

sec-decisions/para1.en:
**Launch as an individual**, with the Hong Kong entity\index{Hong Kong entity}
reachable as a configuration change rather than a rebuild. Under CNY 100,000
annual turnover there is no business-registration requirement, no
foreign-exchange quota consumed, no balance-of-payments filing and no VAT.
sec-decisions/para1.zh: **以个人身份上线**，改用香港实体\index{Hong Kong entity}只需修改配置，无需重新构建。年营业额低于 100,000 元人民币时，无需工商登记，不占用外汇额度，无需国际收支申报，也不缴增值税。

sec-decisions/para2.en:
**Host on Cloudflare Pages**\index{Cloudflare Pages}. The only option with no
bill, no pause, no terms problem and no ICP filing\index{ICP filing}.
sec-decisions/para2.zh: **托管在Cloudflare Pages上**\index{Cloudflare Pages}。这是唯一一个没有账单、不会暂停、没有条款问题且无需 ICP 备案\index{ICP filing}的选项。

sec-decisions/para3.en:
**A page for everything that is shared.** Every work, series and policy has its
own address in both languages; two lines of CSS (`@view-transition`) keep the
calm of a single page when moving between them.
sec-decisions/para3.zh: **凡是会被分享的内容，都有自己的页面。**每件作品、每个系列、每项政策在两种语言中都有独立地址；两行CSS（`@view-transition`）让页面之间切换时仍保有单页的沉静。

sec-decisions/para4.en:
**Self-host the fonts.** 81.7 KB for both families, built from the variable
originals, plus 31.3 KB of italic that is fetched only where an italic is set.
sec-decisions/para4.zh: **字体自行托管。**两个字族共81.7 KB，由可变字体原件生成，另加31.3 KB的斜体，仅在排有斜体的地方才加载。

sec-decisions/para5.en:
**Adopt Priscilla's sage palette** — all of it. The walls are her sage, held at
a lightness that can carry prose; cream is kept for the mat around a painting
and paints no page surface (@sec-sage-ground).
sec-decisions/para5.zh: **采用Priscilla的鼠尾草绿配色**——全部采用。墙色就是她的鼠尾草绿，明度保持在足以承载正文的水平；奶油色只留给画作周围的卡纸，不用于任何页面表面（@sec-sage-ground）。

sec-decisions/para6.en:
**The plates are off, and the type was re-solved for what is left.** The
reading surfaces are transparent, so the field is the only background colour on
the site; the lightness ladder that made those surfaces readable is still in
the token file, still solved, simply not painted (@sec-plates). Reading on a
mid-tone then decided the ink: every text colour was re-solved against the
wall, the lit fall was flattened because its foot could not carry an ink at
all, and the accent was demoted to fills and large text (@sec-ink). The
contrast check treats the wall as an ordinary ground, so all of it blocks the
build.
sec-decisions/para6.zh: **底板已经撤掉，字体也按剩下的条件重新求解。**阅读面是透明的，所以底场是全站唯一的背景色。当初让这些阅读面可读的明度阶梯仍在令牌文件里，也仍然求解过，只是不再上色（@sec-plates）。接着，墨色由“在中间调上阅读”这一条件决定：每一种文字颜色都针对墨色重新求解。光照渐变被压平了，因为它的底端根本承载不了任何墨色。强调色也降级，只用于填充和大号文字（@sec-ink）。对比度检查把墙色当作普通底色处理，所以其中任何一项不达标都会阻断构建。

sec-decisions/para7.en:
**And weight finished what colour could not.** On `#898D76` pure black reaches
6.14:1, so the ladder above is at its ceiling and there is no contrast left to
find; what is left is mass, because a stroke on a mid-tone ground loses to
irradiation in a way it does not on paper. Set as a specimen against the same
text on `#EBEFDB`, Inter at 400 breaks up and at 500 reads as emphasis, and
Fraunces at 400 loses its hairlines outright: the site runs 450 for the sans
and 500 for the serif set as prose, and both go back to 400 the day the plates
come back (@sec-weight).
sec-decisions/para7.zh: **颜色做不到的，由字重补足。**在`#898D76`上，纯黑只能达到6.14:1，所以上面的阶梯已到顶，再也找不出更多对比度。剩下能用的只有笔画的分量：中间调底色上的笔画会被光渗吃掉，这在纸上不会发生。拿同样的文字在`#EBEFDB`上排成样张对照，Inter在 400 时笔画断散，到 500 又读起来像强调；Fraunces在 400 时细线直接消失。因此本站无衬线体用 450，作为正文排的衬线体用 500。等底板恢复的那天，两者都回到 400（@sec-weight）。

sec-decisions/para8.en:
**The ground is a switch, and it is kept in both positions.** `#EBEFDB` is
still the surface that measures best, and the page is not read on it — that is
a decision about what this site looks like, not about what is legible. So
every value the paper ground needs sits commented beside the value the wall
needs, in six pairs, and `check-contrast` reads the plates and solves whichever
is on screen. Neither state can ship unmeasured (@sec-switch-ground).
sec-decisions/para8.zh: **底色是一个开关，两个档位都保留着。**`#EBEFDB`仍然是测量结果最好的表面，但页面不在它上面阅读。这是关于本站外观的决定，与是否易读无关。所以纸色底色需要的每一个值，都以注释形式放在墙色所需的值旁边，共六组；`check-contrast`读取底板，并对屏幕上当前启用的那一种求解。两种状态都不能未经测量就上线（@sec-switch-ground）。

sec-cost/tblcap1.en: Running cost of the recommended build

sec-cost/para1.en:
Payment processing is separate and depends on the entity decision; see
@sec-paying.
sec-cost/para1.zh: 支付处理费用另计，取决于经营主体的决定；见@sec-paying。

sec-visuals/para1.en:
Everything the site is looked at through: its colour, its type, its mark, its
surfaces and edges, the shape of the pages and the review they were put
through. Each is a subsection below, and each carries the research it was
decided on rather than a summary of it — the measurements, the failures, and
what was rejected, so a decision can be re-opened on the evidence that made
it.
sec-visuals/para1.zh: 人们看这个网站时透过的一切：颜色、字体、标志、表面与边缘、页面的形态，以及页面经过的审查。以下每一项各成一小节，每一小节都附上据以作出决定的研究本身，而不是研究摘要：测量数据、失败之处、被否决的方案。这样，任何一个决定都可以依据当初的证据重新讨论。

sec-brief/para1.en:
Priscilla supplied a nine-page draft and, later, a live mockup with a revised
palette, having already built a prototype on Netlify. All three were treated as
the brief. The work here was not to redesign but to find where the drawing and
the medium disagree.
sec-brief/para1.zh: Priscilla先提供了一份九页的草稿，后来又提供了一份调整过配色的在线设计稿，此前她已经在Netlify上做好了一个原型。这三样东西都被当作设计要求。这里的工作不是重新设计，而是找出图稿与媒介不一致的地方。

sec-brief/para2.en:
**How the decisions in this document were taken.** Two things had a vote. The
first is her own work — the draft, the mockup, the prototype and the brand
sheet — which carries the intent, and which this project does not overrule on
taste. The second is measurement: contrast solved rather than judged, layouts
read out of a browser rather than estimated, type set as specimens rather than
chosen from a list. Where the two agree, the artefact wins and nothing is
written down. Where they disagree, three things are established before anything
moves:
sec-brief/para2.zh: **本文中的决定是怎样作出的。**有两样东西拥有表决权。第一是她本人的作品，包括草稿、设计稿、原型和品牌规范页。这些作品承载着她的意图，本项目不在品味问题上推翻它们。第二是测量：对比度靠求解而不是凭感觉判断，版面从浏览器中读出而不是估算，字体排成样张比较而不是从列表里挑选。两者一致时，以作品为准，不另作记录。两者不一致时，先确定三件事，再做任何改动：

sec-brief/item1.en: **what exactly fails**, in numbers — not *the green is hard to read* but *`--muted-ui` drops below 3.0:1 under L\* 91.5, whatever the chroma*;
sec-brief/item1.zh: **究竟哪里不达标**，用数字说明。不是*绿色不好读*，而是*只要低于L\* 91.5，无论彩度多少，`--muted-ui`都会降到3.0:1以下*；

sec-brief/item2.en: **the smallest change that fixes it** — the failing variable and no other, so the drawing survives the correction;
sec-brief/item2.zh: **能修正问题的最小改动**：只改不达标的那一个变量，其他一概不动，让图稿在修正之后依然成立；

sec-brief/item3.en: **whether the alternative can be kept live**, because a decision about how a gallery should look is the artist's to revisit, and a decision that can only be revisited by re-reading this report is a decision she does not really have.
sec-brief/item3.zh: **另一种方案能否保持可用**，因为画廊应当是什么样子，这个决定该由艺术家本人随时重新考虑；而一个只能靠重读这份报告才能重新考虑的决定，她其实并没有真正拥有。

sec-brief/para3.en:
That third test is why several things in this document exist as switches rather
than as settlements: the reading ground (@sec-switch-ground), the entity
(@sec-switch), the shop controls (@sec-next-decisions). Each is one edit in a
data or token file, and each has a check that measures whichever position it is
in, so neither position can ship unmeasured.
sec-brief/para3.zh: 正因为第三条检验，本文中有几样东西是以开关而非定案的形式存在的：阅读底色（@sec-switch-ground）、实体（@sec-switch）、商店控件（@sec-next-decisions）。每一项都只需在一个数据文件或令牌文件中改一处，而且每一项都有一个检查，无论它处于哪个位置都会测量，所以哪个位置都不可能未经测量就上线。

sec-brief/para4.en: The disagreements were mostly about contrast.

sec-colour/para1.en:
Priscilla's mockup moves the site from white to a sage-green world: a dark
brown masthead bar, warm brown text, terracotta, and cream plates behind the
paintings. Two of her decisions were already right and are kept exactly as
drawn — the warm browns, and a **filled** terracotta button.
sec-colour/para1.zh: Priscilla的设计稿把网站从白色带入一个鼠尾草绿的世界：深棕色的页头栏、暖棕色的文字、赤陶色，以及画作背后的奶油色衬板。她有两个决定本来就是对的，完全按原稿保留——暖棕色系，以及一个**实心**赤陶色按钮。

sec-colour/caption1.en: The palette as built. Each value is read from the project's token file, not transcribed.
sec-colour/caption1.zh: 实际建成的配色。每个数值都直接读自项目的令牌文件，而非手工抄录。

sec-sage/head.en: What could not be adopted as drawn

sec-sage/para1.en:
Body text on the sage does not pass, and the accent on sage is worse than the
value it was replacing.
sec-sage/para1.zh: 鼠尾草绿上的正文无法通过，而鼠尾草绿上的强调色比它所取代的那个值还要差。

sec-sage/caption1.en: Why the sage carries no text. The three red bars are Priscilla's mockup as drawn; the draft's original failure is included for scale.
sec-sage/caption1.zh: 为什么鼠尾草绿上不放文字。三条红色柱是Priscilla设计稿的原样；草稿最初的不合格结果也列在其中，作为参照。

sec-sage/callout1.en: The resolution was already in her own mockup
sec-sage/callout1.zh: 解决办法其实早已在她自己的设计稿里

sec-sage/para2.en:
She sets the paintings on light cream plates against the sage. So sage becomes
the **field** and a light plate the **reading surface** — the whole content
column is a sheet mounted on sage, which is what a gallery does to a work on
paper anyway.
sec-sage/para2.zh: 她把画作放在浅奶油色衬板上，衬在鼠尾草绿之上。于是鼠尾草绿成为**色场**，浅色衬板成为**阅读面**——整个内容栏是一张裱在鼠尾草绿上的纸，而这本来就是画廊处理纸本作品的方式。

sec-sage/para3.en: Her green stays dominant at the margins, and nothing sets text on the field.
sec-sage/para3.zh: 她的绿色在四周边缘保持主导，而任何文字都不放在色场上。

sec-sage/para4.en:
The sheet was cream while the palette was cream. Her brief moved it to sage
(@sec-sage-ground) and then asked for no reading ground at all (@sec-plates);
what the page shows is the second of those, with the first kept live beside it
(@sec-switch-ground).
sec-sage/para4.zh: 配色是奶油色的时候，这张纸也是奶油色。她的要求先把它改为鼠尾草绿（@sec-sage-ground），随后又要求完全不要阅读底色（@sec-plates）；页面现在呈现的是后者，前者则在旁边保持可用（@sec-switch-ground）。

sec-sage-ground/head.zh: 以鼠尾草绿作为阅读底色

sec-sage-ground/para1.en: *Her brief: cream for the art, sage for everything else. What that turned out to require.*
sec-sage-ground/para1.zh: *她的要求：奶油色留给艺术品，其余一切用鼠尾草绿。结果发现这需要做些什么。*

sec-sage-ground/para2.en:
The brief for this pass was one line: restrict cream to the backgrounds of the
art pieces, and put everything else on sage and its variations. That is a
bigger request than it sounds, because @sec-sage is the reason the reading was
on cream in the first place — her sage measures 2.35:1 under body text.
sec-sage-ground/para2.zh: 这一轮的要求只有一句话：把奶油色限定在艺术品的背景上，其余一切都放在鼠尾草绿及其变化色上。这比听上去要大得多，因为@sec-sage正是当初阅读内容放在奶油色上的原因——她的鼠尾草绿在正文下测得2.35:1。

sec-sage-ground/para3.en:
So the first question is not *which* sage but **what the failure was actually
about**. It is answerable by measurement rather than by taste. Solving every
foreground the site sets on a reading surface — nine of them, at their own
floors — over a grid of candidate grounds in the plane of the field's own hue
gives @fig-sage-ground, and the finding is the shape of the boundary:
sec-sage-ground/para3.zh: 所以第一个问题不是*哪一种*鼠尾草绿，而是**那次不合格究竟是因为什么**。这个问题可以靠测量回答，而不是靠品味。把网站在阅读面上使用的每一种前景色——共九种，各按其自身的下限——放在色场自身色相平面内的一组候选底色上逐一求解，得到@fig-sage-ground，而结论就在边界的形状里：

sec-sage-ground/quote1.en: The line is **flat**. A reading ground fails on **lightness** and on nothing else. Below L\* 91.5 the binding pair is `--muted-ui` at 3.0:1 — an icon stroke, not prose — and above it, **chroma is free**: a ground can carry the field's full chroma of 0.043 and `--muted-ui` still measures 3.05:1.
sec-sage-ground/quote1.zh: 这条线是**平的**。阅读底色不合格只因为**明度**，别无其他。在L\* 91.5以下，起约束作用的一对是`--muted-ui`，处于3.0:1——那是图标描边，不是正文——而在此之上，**彩度不受限制**：底色可以带上色场的全部彩度0.043，`--muted-ui`依然测得3.05:1。

sec-sage-ground/caption1.en: Where a reading ground may live. Every cell is a real colour at the field's hue; the veiled region is what `check-contrast.mjs` refuses.
sec-sage-ground/caption1.zh: 阅读底色可以落在哪里。每个格子都是色场色相上的一种真实颜色；被遮罩的区域是`check-contrast.mjs`所拒绝的。

sec-sage-ground/para4.en:
Which makes the move obvious and cheap: **keep the lightness ladder that was
already measured safe, and rotate its chroma onto the field's hue.** The three
grounds do not move up or down, so not one of the ~60 pairs the contrast check
solves had to be re-solved. They are better than they were:
sec-sage-ground/para4.zh: 于是做法就显而易见，而且代价很低：**保留那条早已测得安全的明度阶梯，把它的彩度转到色场的色相上。**三种底色都没有变亮或变暗，所以对比度检查所求解的约60对组合中，没有一对需要重新求解。它们比以前更好：

sec-sage-ground/tblcap1.en: The three reading grounds, before and after. Not one foreground token moved.
sec-sage-ground/tblcap1.zh: 三种阅读底色，改动前后对比。没有一个前景令牌改动过。

sec-sage-ground/para5.en:
The old names — warm, violet, blue — were inherited from washes that had been
gone for months; all three were cream. They are now named for the only thing
that separates them, which is lightness.
sec-sage-ground/para5.zh: 旧名称——暖、紫、蓝——沿用自几个月前就已撤掉的色晕；这三种其实都是奶油色。现在它们按唯一能区分彼此的东西命名，也就是明度。

sec-sage-ground/para6.en:
Every ratio in that table is measured with the **ink of that morning**. The ink
ladder was re-solved the same evening, for a wall rather than a plate
(@sec-ink), so a plate now carries far more than the table claims — `--body` on
`--wash-pale` is 14.37:1, not 5.78:1. The comparison is left as it was made,
because what it was demonstrating is that moving the grounds onto the field's
hue cost nothing, and that is still exactly what it shows.
sec-sage-ground/para6.zh: 表中每一个对比度，都是用**那天上午的墨色**测得的。墨色阶梯当晚就重新求解了，针对的是墙面而不是衬板（@sec-ink），所以现在衬板上的对比度远高于表中所写——`--body`在`--wash-pale`上是14.37:1，而不是5.78:1。这组比较保留当时的原样，因为它要证明的是：把底色移到色场的色相上不付出任何代价，而这一点它至今仍然准确地表明。

sec-sage-ground/para7.en:
Every value in that table is still in the token file, still solved and still
checked. None of them is currently **painted**: @sec-plates.
sec-sage-ground/para7.zh: 表中每一个数值都还在令牌文件里，仍然经过求解，仍然受到检查。但目前没有一个真正被**涂上**：@sec-plates。

sec-sage-ground/para8.en:
**Then where does cream go?** It keeps the job it was drawn for in her mockup
and gives up the one the build invented for it. Cream paints:
sec-sage-ground/para8.zh: **那么奶油色去哪儿了？**它保留她在设计稿中为它设定的职责，放弃构建替它发明的那一个。奶油色用来涂：

sec-sage-ground/item1.en: the **mat** around every painting, and the same mat around the video and the thumbnails — a board is a different material from a wall, and one step of hue is what says so: against `--wash-deep` the mat is dE 1.8 in OKLab, a boundary you can see and cannot name;
sec-sage-ground/item1.zh: 每幅画周围的**卡纸**，以及视频和缩略图周围同样的卡纸——卡纸和墙是不同的材质，色相上差一级就是在说明这一点：相对于`--wash-deep`，卡纸在 OKLab 中的 dE 为 1.8，是一条看得见却说不出的边界；

sec-sage-ground/item2.en: the box that holds an image before its bytes arrive;
sec-sage-ground/item2.zh: 图片数据到达之前承载它的方框；

sec-sage-ground/item3.en: light **ink on the dark bar** — the wordmark, the navigation, the 12 % wash under a hovered control;
sec-sage-ground/item3.zh: **深色栏上的浅色墨**——字标、导航，以及悬停控件下 12 % 的色晕；

sec-sage-ground/item4.en: the focus halo, which has to survive being drawn over a dark painting.
sec-sage-ground/item4.zh: 焦点光晕，它必须在深色画作上方绘制时依然清晰可见。

sec-sage-ground/para9.en:
It paints no ground that anyone reads on. `check-review.mjs` L-01 holds that
by listing every rule allowed to paint cream — fifteen of them — and failing on
a sixteenth, so adding one is a decision rather than a slip.
sec-sage-ground/para9.zh: 它不涂任何供人阅读的底色。`check-review.mjs` L-01 守住这一点的办法是：列出所有允许涂奶油色的规则——共十五条——出现第十六条就判定失败，这样新增一条就成了一个决定，而不是一次疏忽。

sec-sage-ground/para10.en:
One new token came out of it. The frosted plate behind the contact panel was
`--paper` at 72 %, which on the palest ground made it *the same colour as the
thing it was laid on*. It is now `--wash-lift`, one step lighter than every
ground, so the plate is visible on all three and still cannot darken what is
read on it.
sec-sage-ground/para10.zh: 由此只产生了一个新令牌。联系面板背后的磨砂衬板原本是 72 % 的`--paper`，在最浅的底色上，这让它*和它所铺在上面的东西同色*。现在它是`--wash-lift`，比每一种底色都浅一级，因此在三种底色上都看得见，同时仍然不会让其上被阅读的内容变暗。

sec-plates/para1.en: *The same brief, one step further: no reading ground at all.*
sec-plates/para1.zh: *同样的要求，再进一步：完全不要阅读底色。*

sec-plates/para2.en:
The brief for this one was also a line: make the backgrounds behind the text
transparent, so that nothing of `#EBEFDB` shows anywhere and the only
background colour on the site is the sage. It is @sec-sage-ground read
backwards. That pass asked what a reading ground may be; this one asks what is
left when there is none.
sec-plates/para2.zh: 这一次的要求同样只有一句话：把文字后面的背景设为透明，让`#EBEFDB`在任何地方都不再露出，网站上唯一的背景色就是鼠尾草绿。这是把@sec-sage-ground倒过来读。那一轮问的是阅读底色可以是什么；这一轮问的是没有阅读底色时还剩下什么。

sec-plates/para3.en:
**Nothing was deleted to do it,** because the request was for a switch rather
than a demolition (@sec-brief). Every surface that is read paints a token of
its own, and those tokens are what is transparent:
sec-plates/para3.zh: **为此没有删除任何东西，**因为要求的是一个开关，而不是拆除（@sec-brief）。每一个被阅读的表面都涂着自己专属的令牌，而被设为透明的正是这些令牌：

sec-plates/tblcap1.en: What paints a surface that is read
sec-plates/tblcap1.zh: 是什么在涂被阅读的表面

sec-plates/cell9.en: Works, How to Buy, the hero
sec-plates/cell9.zh: 作品、购买方式、首屏大图

sec-plates/para4.en:
Putting the paper back is those four values and one more, with no rule touched:
`--plate-sheet` and `--plate-pale` to `var(--wash-pale)`, `--plate-mid` and
`--plate-deep` to their own washes, and `--edge-breath` to 20%. Any other value
is equally available — one section can be given a ground of its own, in a
colour that is not in the ladder at all, without opening the stylesheet.

sec-plates/para5.en:
Two details are worth the words. **A band's ends are the plates of the sections
either side of it, not the washes those plates happen to hold** — which is what
keeps the finding of @sec-soft-options true through a change of plate: a
boundary cannot fade to the wrong neighbour because it does not know what
colour its neighbours are. And `--edge-breath` goes to **0%**: a band exists to
join two grounds through the field, and with no grounds to join, a fifth of the
sage laid over the sage would be invisible in the middle of the fall and a
faint horizontal smudge at either end of it. The bands keep their 9 rem, which
is section spacing, and paint nothing.

sec-plates/para6.en:
**The lightbox is the exception, and has to be.** A backdrop exists to hide the
page behind an opened work, so transparent is not available to it. The
equivalent of letting the field through is the field itself, at the same 94%.

sec-plates/para7.en:
**What it costs.** The washes exist for a reason, and it should not be possible
to switch them off without reading the bill. Every foreground the site sets on
a reading surface is now read on the field, and the field is the one surface in
this palette that was never solved for text. It is also lit — `--field` at the
top of the fall, `--field-deep` at the foot — so both columns below are real
grounds on the same page, not a range.

sec-plates/tblcap2.en: The bill for switching the plates off, against the ink as the cream palette had left it. Every figure here is superseded by the re-solve of @sec-ink; it is kept because it is what the re-solve had to beat.

sec-plates/para8.en:
That was quietness bought with contrast, which is the one thing this report
opens by forbidding: the draft failed its review because every call to action
was `#A19E97` at 2.67:1, and `--body` on the field was worse than that at both
ends of the page.

sec-plates/para9.en:
It stays in the record in those terms because it is what made the type re-solve
necessary, and what the re-solve had to beat. It did: the ladder of @tbl-ink
clears every floor on the wall, the fall was flattened because its foot could
not carry an ink at all, and the accent was demoted to fills and large text.
The plates being off is no longer a contrast debt; it is a constraint the type
is now solved inside.

sec-plates/para10.en:
**What the check does about it.** `check-contrast.mjs` reads the plate tokens,
and when any of them is transparent it adds the **wall** to the grounds every
foreground is solved against — so with the plates off, `--field` is checked
exactly as a plate is, and a regression on it blocks the build. Before the
re-solve of @sec-ink the same block could only *print* the bill and decline to
certify the page, because no ladder passed; now that one does, the check binds
rather than reports. Beside the verdict it still prints the headroom — how much
of the wall's own budget each rung is using — because the budget is what will
bite if the wall moves again.

sec-plates/para11.en:
`check-review.mjs` L-05 holds the mechanism rather than the value: the five
plates must be declared, the five rules that paint a ground must name them —
the bands are G-06's — and **no rule anywhere may name a wash directly**. A hardcoded `--wash-pale` in a rule is how
a surface falls out of the switch and stops being reversible, which is the only
way this decision could quietly become permanent.

sec-plates/para12.en:
**What is still painted.** Cream keeps the mat, the image box and the bar
(@sec-sage-ground, L-01), and the frosted contact panel keeps its `--wash-lift`
at 72%. That panel is now the one plate left on the site, and the arithmetic of
@sec-soft-glass has turned around with it: over the field it composites to
`#D3D6C4`, where `--body` measures **4.58:1** at the top of the fall and 4.23 at
the foot. The plate that could only ever make text paler is now the most
legible reading surface on the site.

sec-plates/para13.en:
**The mount goes with the plate.** A shadow and a rim light are what say a
sheet is lying *on* the field rather than being a hole cut in it; with
`--plate-sheet` transparent there is no sheet lying there, and the pair draws a
1240 px rectangle, filled with the field's own green, whose edges correspond to
nothing anybody can see. That reads as a rendering fault rather than as a
mount. It is `--mount-sheet`, `none` on the wall, and it returns with the
paper.

sec-switch-ground/head.en: The switch, kept in both positions

sec-switch-ground/para1.en:
`#EBEFDB` is the surface that measures best and the site is not read on it.
That is a decision about what this gallery looks like rather than about what is
legible, and a decision of that kind should be reversible by someone who is not
holding this document.

sec-switch-ground/para2.en:
So the paper ground is kept, commented, beside the wall ground, in six pairs.
Five are in `tokens.css` and one in `base.css`; the file's own header indexes
all six, because a switch scattered across six places is a slow switch however
well each place is commented.

sec-switch-ground/tblcap1.en: The ground switch. Nothing else has to be re-solved: the ink ladder clears its floors on both.

sec-switch-ground/para3.en:
Three of those six are the same observation in different materials. A mid-tone
ground takes strokes, so the weights move (@sec-weight). A decorative line's
quietness is a *ratio* and not a colour, so both the hairline and the hatch
move: `#D6DAC4` measures 1.22:1 on `#EBEFDB` and 2.39 on the wall — twice as
present, and plainly a line — while the hatch was measured at 7% on sage at
L\* 57 and carries half again the contrast on a ground at L\* 93. And a
transparent sheet has nothing to cast a shadow from, so the mount goes.

sec-switch-ground/para4.en:
`check-contrast` reads the plates and solves whichever ground is on screen, so
neither position can ship unmeasured. Both were built and checked before this
was written: with the paper values uncommented the site builds, the contrast
gate solves `#EBEFDB` instead of the wall, and every assertion, readiness test
and painting box passes — then back to the wall, clean.

sec-wall/head.en: The wall, re-solved against the prototype

sec-wall/para1.en: *The wall, once it became the page.*

sec-wall/para2.en:
With the plates transparent the field stopped being a margin and became the
whole page, and at that size it read fresher and lighter than the site
Priscilla had been looking at — the Netlify prototype she had built before this
work started. The brief was to make it *more vintage, and a little less
saturated, like the prototype*.

sec-wall/para3.en:
So the prototype was measured rather than matched by eye. Its wall is a **flat
`#868E6E`**, and the measurement contains a surprise worth keeping in the
record:

sec-wall/tblcap1.en: The three greens, in OKLCh. What reads as vintage in the prototype is the lightness; its chroma is *higher* than her sheet's, not lower.

sec-wall/para4.en:
**The rest of the capture was sampled too**, because moving a wall toward the
prototype is only an improvement if what stands on it already agrees — and it
does, with one deliberate exception:

sec-wall/tblcap2.en: Everything else measured off the same capture. dE is OKLab.

sec-wall/cell23.en: dE 9.1, and **not adopted**: cream on the prototype's lighter terracotta is 3.83:1, which fails a button label. The deeper value carries 5.64:1

sec-wall/cell26.en: the prototype's wall is **flat**; the site keeps its lit fall, which is a decision of its own (@sec-soft-glass)

sec-wall/para5.en:
The new wall sits dE **1.38** from the prototype's, where the sheet's sage sat
at 4.61 — so the page is now within a step of the green Priscilla had been
looking at, and the step that remains is the saturation she asked to come down.

sec-wall/para6.en:
The wall therefore takes the prototype's **lightness** and the asked-for step
down in **saturation** — 21 % under the sheet's chroma, 28 % under the
prototype's — and does not move in **hue**, because the three reading grounds
are locked to the field's own hue within two degrees (`check-review.mjs` L-02),
and rotating a wall nobody reads on would have meant re-solving four grounds
that are not currently painted. `--field-deep` follows it down by the same
interval, so the fall the field carries is unchanged in shape.

sec-wall/callout1.en: The first departure from the sheet

sec-wall/para7.en:
Her brand sheet states **Primary (Sage Green) `#969B7D`** and **Deep Green
`#737C61`**, and until this pass those were `--field` and `--field-deep`
*exactly* — the palette's one perfect quotation. They are not any more.

sec-wall/para8.en:
The reason is that the wall changed job. A colour chosen as the margin around
a sheet of paper is not automatically the right colour for every pixel of
every page, and that is what it became when the plates went transparent. Her
values remain the brand's: the mark is drawn against them (`scripts/mark.mjs`),
the report's sheet table quotes them, and print uses them.

sec-wall/para9.en:
What the site cannot have is two greens that are nearly the same. `L-06`
therefore solves the two places the wall is written out in full — the lightbox
backdrop's fallback for engines without `color-mix()`, and the installed app's
splash ground in the web manifest, which is JSON and cannot hold a token —
against `--field` itself, so a wall that moves again cannot leave a stale copy
of itself behind in a lightbox or on a splash screen.

sec-wall/para10.en:
**It cost contrast, and the type paid it.** A darker wall under the same ink is
a smaller ratio: `--ink` went 4.70 → **3.96** and `--body` 2.35 → **1.98**,
which is the state @tbl-plates-cost records. That bill is what forced the ink
ladder to be re-solved the same evening — a new value for every text colour, a
flat wall instead of a lit fall, and an accent that no longer sets small text
(@sec-ink). With the plates painted none of it would have signified; it
signified because they are off, which is the other half of the same decision.

sec-panel/head.en: The panel, and what that green admits

sec-panel/para1.en:
Priscilla asked for one section to be painted: About, in **"Dark Sage"
#727A5C**, a darker cut of the wall, so it reads as a panel set into the page
rather than as another stretch of it. The plates made that a one-line change —
it is exactly the case the indirection was built for (@sec-plates) — and the
colour made it the most constrained surface on the site.

sec-panel/para2.en:
**That green is the exact centre of the mid-tone squeeze.** The wall is a
mid-tone with a ceiling (@sec-ink); this is a mid-tone with barely a budget at
all. Measured:

sec-panel/para3.en:
Every rung of the ladder fails on it, in both polarities, and the whole of
colour space has about **3 % of headroom**: nothing can do better than pure
black's 4.65. So either the colour moves or the ink does, and the colour was
the request.

sec-panel/para4.en:
`--ink-deep` **#080301** is what the panel is set in: 4.55:1 on the green,
5.99:1 on the wall, the ladder's own hue, and the only value that clears the
floor with anything to spare. Lightening the green instead was solved and
rejected — the ladder needs a ground at Y ≥ 0.249 and the wall is already at
0.257, so the darkest sage that carries `--muted` is within one L\* step of
the wall and would not read as a panel at all.

sec-panel/para5.en:
**What it costs is the section's tonal hierarchy.** Everything inside the
panel is that one ink: the heading, the prose, the caption under the portrait,
the link and its hover. There is no quieter grey for a caption on this ground
and no terracotta to hover into, so size, weight, small caps and the underline
carry what colour used to. That is stated in the stylesheet beside the rule,
in `--ink-deep` beside the token, and asserted by N-03 — and the contrast
check solves the panel as a ground of its own, so nothing else can be painted
on it without being solved for it first.

sec-trap/para1.en:
`#767676` is the canonical "lightest grey that passes on white". On pure white
it passes at 4.54:1, with 0.04 to spare. Warm the ground at all and it fails.

sec-trap/para2.en:
This caught the project three times — twice in tokens written specifically to
avoid it. The response was to stop checking by eye: `scripts/check-contrast.mjs`
recomputes every token against **the darkest ground it is ever painted on** and
fails the build on a regression.

sec-type/para1.en: Two open-source variable faces, self-hosted: Fraunces\index{Fraunces} and Inter.

sec-type/tblcap1.en: Font build, measured rather than estimated

sec-type/para2.en:
Two corrections came out of running the build rather than reading about it.
The draft sets Fraunces at six optical sizes — 16.0, 16.8, 21.6, 27.2, 30.4 and
38.4 — so the `opsz` axis must stay live; pinning it saves 19 KB and flattens
the optical sizing the design depends on. And Fraunces' `WONK` axis defaults to
**1, not 0**; pinning it to 0 changes the letterforms to save 140 bytes.

sec-ink/head.en: The ink, re-solved for the wall

sec-ink/para1.en:
*Decision of 20 September 2026, and the reason the type section carries a
colour problem at all.*

sec-ink/para2.en:
Type colour is normally settled once with the palette. It had to be re-solved
here because the ground moved twice in a day: the plates went transparent, and
then the wall went darker — @sec-plates and @sec-wall — and between them every
word on the site ended up on a **mid-tone**, which is the one kind of ground
that is hard for text in both directions.

sec-ink/tblcap1.en: What the wall can hold at all. A mid-tone is squeezed from both ends: too dark for light text, too light for anything but a very dark ink.

sec-ink/cell8.en: **light text is impossible** — it cannot reach 4.5:1 at any value

sec-ink/para3.en:
Her warm brown `#3A2B22` is Y 0.0274. On a cream plate it is 11.45:1 and on the
wall it is 3.96:1 — which is a heading colour and nothing else. So the ladder
keeps her **hue exactly** and drops its lightness until each rung clears the
floor it has to carry:

sec-ink/tblcap2.en: The ink ladder, re-solved. "On a plate" is `--wash-pale`, for when the plates are painted again.

sec-ink/para4.en: Three things follow from that table, and none of them is a preference.

sec-ink/para5.en:
**The lit fall had to go flat.** The field ran from `--field` at the top to
`--field-deep` at the foot, fixed, so the page was lit. At the foot,
`--field-deep` holds **4.10:1 for pure black** — there is no ink, of any
colour, that a paragraph could be set in there. One wall is one contrast
problem and it is solvable; two walls are not. The fall returns with the
plates, and `--field-deep` stays defined meanwhile: it is the sheet's Deep
Green, and the mark is drawn against it.

sec-ink/para6.en:
**The accent cannot set small text.** No red-brown that is still a red-brown
reaches 4.5:1 on this ground — at that floor it is a maroon indistinguishable
from the ink. `--sanguine` is therefore solved to the 3:1 tier and paints
fills, rules and large accents only: the three-line drop cap on About keeps it,
the contact panel's top border keeps it, the scale diagram's strokes keep it.
Everything smaller takes `--sanguine-deep` at 4.61:1, and **links take the
ink** — the underline was already doing the work of distinguishing them
(technique G183), and the hover is what carries the accent now.

sec-ink/para7.en:
**The ink is darker than the bar.** `--ink` and `--bar` were the same warm
brown, which was one of the palette's neatnesses. The bar is still hers and
still carries cream at 11.45:1, but the ink had to leave it: `#3A2B22` cannot
be read on sage, and the bar cannot be darkened without leaving the brown the
prototype and the sheet agree on (@tbl-proto).

sec-ink/para8.en:
**What holds it.** `check-contrast.mjs` now solves every one of these against
the wall as an ordinary ground rather than printing a bill beside them — with
the plates off, `wall` is in the grounds list, so a regression blocks the build
like any other. `check-review.mjs` L-07 holds the accent's division of labour
by naming the two rules allowed to set `--sanguine` as text, and it earned its
place immediately: it caught a breadcrumb and a series card still setting the
accent at caption size.

sec-ink/para9.en:
And the principle the whole ladder rests on is the one the report opens with —
*buy quietness with size and whitespace, never with contrast*. The colour
budget on this wall is spent; what is left to build hierarchy with is size,
weight and space, which is what the scale (@sec-scale) is for.

sec-italic/head.en: The italic the site was faking

sec-italic/para1.en:
The site sets italic in four places — the hero's Dutch original, the Tribute
epigraph, and every work title, both in the list and as an `h1` — and shipped
no italic file, so the browser slanted the roman by 12° in all four. A synthetic
oblique of a high-contrast serif is a poor imitation of a drawing that already
exists: Fraunces' italic is a different letter, not a tilted one, with a
single-storey *a*, a cursive *e* and a −16° angle the letterforms were made for.

sec-italic/para2.en:
It is now a real file, and the axes are narrowed harder than the roman's
because its uses are known exactly: `opsz` 14–30 covers every size an italic is
actually set at, and one weight, because no italic on this site is bold. That
is **32,080 bytes**; keeping 400–700 would have been 58,344 for nothing. It is
deliberately *not* preloaded — nothing above the fold waits on it — and
`font-synthesis-style: none` now says the browser may not invent the style
anywhere else either, including for the Chinese face, which has no italic and
should not be given a slanted one.

sec-about-type/head.en: About, set as a book page

sec-about-type/para1.en:
About is the only page on the site that is nothing but prose. It was set in the
interface face, at interface size, in a column the same shape as How to Buy —
a form with an essay in it.

sec-about-type/para2.en:
The first question was whether it needed a new typeface, and the answer is on
the record with numbers rather than as a preference:

sec-about-type/item1.en: **A third family** was rejected on the same grounds as @sec-type: every render-blocking file is another thing to go wrong in a Chinese TCP handshake.

sec-about-type/item2.en: **Fraunces' `SOFT` axis**, kept live, would soften the terminals — and take the roman from 51,868 to **91,304 bytes**, +76 % on a preloaded file, for one page's worth of prettiness.

sec-about-type/item3.en: **Old-style figures and small caps** were the obvious next reach, and Fraunces simply has neither: its whole `GSUB` is `case`, `liga`, `rvrn`, `ss01`. So "10 %" is set in the lining figures the face draws, and nothing is faked.

sec-about-type/para3.en:
What the page is set in, then, is the face the site already preloads — at the
one size where that face is the same **reading size** as the sans it replaces.
That size is not a matter of judgement either. Measured off the shipped
subsets, at their own optical sizes:

sec-about-type/caption1.en: Why 19.2 px. A serif set at the sans's point size makes a page of prose quietly smaller; x-height is what a reader sees.

sec-about-type/para4.en:
19.2 px is also where the type scale already put it — the hero halved
(@tbl-scale) — so the page gains a reading size without inventing a step.

sec-about-type/para5.en:
Four moves, three of which cost nothing to download: the display face at
`--size-read` with `opsz` tied to it; a **lede**, the first paragraph at
`--size-mark` in `--ink`, so the page opens with a voice; a **drop cap** of
three lines in sanguine, behind an `@supports (initial-letter: 3)` test so it
simply does not happen where the property is unsupported; and the van Gogh
quotation that closes the page set in the **real italic**, which `build.js`
marks by wrapping the quoted span.

sec-about-type/para6.en:
Two details are about the Chinese page, and both are refusals. It gets no drop
cap and no italic, because neither is a Chinese typographic device and both
would be synthesised. And it is **not** set in `--font-display`: that stack
begins with the subset Noto Serif SC, which carries only the ~100 CJK glyphs
that appear in display positions, so a page of Chinese prose set in it would
render some characters in Noto and the rest in the system face — one paragraph,
two typefaces. `--font-read-cjk` is a stack of system serifs instead, so the
Chinese About page gets a book face for nothing, and gets it consistently.

sec-cjk/head.en: The Chinese face, and what is not served

sec-cjk/para1.en:
The display face is subset to the characters that actually appear in display
positions — headings, work titles, UI labels: **34 KB, cut from a 24 MB face.**
`unicode-range` gates the fetch, so an English page never downloads a byte of
it, and a character Priscilla adds before the next build falls through to the
system face rather than rendering as tofu.

sec-cjk/para2.en:
Chinese **body prose is deliberately not webfont-served**. The system serif is
already on the device and costs nothing across a border, which matters more on
this site than a uniform drawing does.

sec-cjk/para3.en:
That decision has one trap in it, and the token file carries the note: the
Chinese About page cannot be set in `--font-display`, because that stack begins
with the subset Noto Serif SC. A page of Chinese prose set in it would render
the ~100 subset characters in Noto and everything else in the system face —
one paragraph, two typefaces. It takes `--font-read-cjk` instead, which is
system serifs all the way down, so the book page is consistent and free
(@sec-about-type).

sec-scale/para1.en:
Not the golden ratio. The one proportional system in Leonardo's own hand, on
the *Vitruvian Man* sheet, is whole-number fractions of height.

sec-scale/tblcap1.en: Type scale, and how close Priscilla's draft already was

sec-scale-fluid/head.en: The three display steps move with the column

sec-scale-fluid/para1.en:
Those three heads are 1.14 and 1.17 apart, which is under the interval at
which a reader sees a *level* rather than a size, and then there is a 1.71 drop
to body with nothing in between. All of it was fixed px, so the motto was
38.4 px on a 390 px phone and 38.4 px on a 1920 px display: the layout grew and
the voice did not.

sec-scale-fluid/para2.en:
The fractions are kept as the **ends** of each step rather than as one value.
Every rung still lands on the draft's own size at the width it was measured at,
and moves between them with the column:

sec-scale-fluid/tblcap1.en: The ladder as rendered, in px

sec-scale-fluid/para3.en:
What bounds the top end is the motto, which is set as written and may never be
re-wrapped (@sec-band). `opsz` stops being pinned with the sizes: with no one
size to pin it to, `font-optical-sizing` drives the axis from the size actually
used — which is what pinning it was approximating, and the reason the axis was
kept live in the font build at all.

sec-weight/head.en: Weight, which is the ground's business

sec-weight/para1.en:
A size ladder is not the whole of setting type on a mid-tone ground. With the
ink already at the wall's ceiling — pure black reaches 6.14:1 on `#898D76`, so
@sec-ink has taken every point of contrast there is — the remaining variable is
stroke weight, because a dark letter on a lit ground loses to irradiation in a
way it does not on paper. The ground bleeds into the letter; the remedy is
mass, not colour.

sec-weight/para2.en:
It was decided by specimen rather than by rule: the same paragraph, set on
`--field` in `--body`, against the same text on `#EBEFDB`.

sec-weight/cell4.en: Stems break up, the counters close — as originally shipped

sec-weight/cell6.en: Solid, and still unmistakably a regular — **adopted**

sec-weight/cell8.en: Reads as emphasis rather than as running text

sec-weight/tblcap1.en: What the wall does to a stroke, measured by eye against paper

sec-weight/para3.en:
The serif needs more of the correction than the sans, which is what the
specimen was for: Fraunces' thin strokes are the first thing this ground takes.
Headings stay at 400 — display sizes pay almost nothing to irradiation — but
through a token, so a ground that moves moves them too.

sec-weight/para4.en:
Both go back to 400 on paper. The correction belongs to the ground, not to the
typeface, which is why it is one of the six pairs in @sec-switch-ground rather
than a new fact about Inter. `font-synthesis-weight: none` was already set, so
450 is a real interpolation of Inter's live axis and the system CJK face this
stack falls through to rounds to a weight it actually has, rather than being
emboldened by the rasteriser.

sec-mark/para1.en:
The site had a wordmark and no mark. On a business whose entire acquisition
motion is a link in an Instagram or a WeChat bio, the surfaces that render
most often are a browser tab, a share card and an avatar — and none of them
can render a wordmark.

sec-mark/para2.en:
The mark it now carries is Priscilla's own: an interlocking **SC** monogram,
drawn, with a prototype sheet that arrives with a construction, a palette, four
variations and a minimum size already worked out. **The site uses that
artwork itself** — her drawing, cropped and resized, never redrawn.

sec-mark-constraint/head.en: The constraint that used to decide it

sec-mark-constraint/para1.en:
The wordmark translates: *Senso Comune Gallery* in English, 常识画廊\index{wordmark} in
Chinese. A favicon, by contrast, is chosen by **origin**, not by page: one file
serves both URL trees, so a site cannot ship one mark per locale however much
it would like to.

sec-mark-constraint/para2.en:
The first mark took that to its conclusion and carried no letterforms at all —
a work on a wall, three rectangles and a hanging line — on the argument that
`SC` is not the initials of 常识画廊 and would therefore serve one audience
and decorate the other.

sec-mark-constraint/callout1.en: Why that argument no longer holds

sec-mark-constraint/para3.en:
Finding C-04 asked for the Latin wordmark to be kept constant in both locales,
and was **closed by decision**: Priscilla keeps 常识画廊 as the Chinese name,
because it reads as native to the domestic audience and that is worth more
than one lockup in two languages.

sec-mark-constraint/para4.en:
That decision is what frees the mark. A monogram is not a translation of a
name — it is a *device* that stands beside one, and a device does not have to
be readable as the name it accompanies any more than a crest does. The Latin
device beside the Chinese name is the arrangement most international houses
use in China. What is not allowed is a mark that says a *different* name in
each locale, and the build asserts that the lockup is byte-identical on the
English and Chinese homepages.

sec-mark-sheet/caption1.en: The prototype sheet, reproduced as supplied — `brand/brand-sheet.png`.

sec-mark-sheet/para1.en:
Construction and proportion, the hatching detail, the four variations, clear
space and minimum size, the four brand colours, and the horizontal and vertical
lockups.

sec-mark-sheet/caption2.en: The preferred option, reproduced as supplied — `brand/mark-lockup.png`.

sec-mark-sheet/para2.en:
This is the artwork the site uses: the monogram with its construction lines,
over the wordmark. Everything the build ships is a crop and a resize of this
one file.

sec-mark-sheet/para3.en:
Both files live in `brand/`, unmodified, and are pinned by hash: re-exporting
or tidying either one fails the build and has to be a decision rather than an
accident. They arrived at `dist/archive/logo/`, which is build output and is
gitignored, so keeping them meant moving them somewhere the repository keeps.

sec-mark-notes/head.en: The notes on the sheet, and what each one costs

sec-mark-notes/para1.en:
Every row's left column is the sheet's own wording. The right column is what
it means once the mark has to live in a browser tab, on a phone masthead and
in this document.

sec-mark-notes/tblcap1.en: The sheet's specification, and the issue against each

sec-mark-notes/cell2.en: What it costs, and what was done

sec-mark-notes/cell4.en: Adopted as drawn — the artwork *is* the construction, so nothing has to be re-derived. The number only became a question when the mark was being rebuilt rather than used; see @sec-mark-construction

sec-mark-notes/cell6.en: As above. Taken literally in a *rebuild* it makes the S fall to about the C's x-height; in Priscilla's own drawing the S is visibly larger than 1/1.618 of the C, which is why the drawing reads and a literal reconstruction did not

sec-mark-notes/cell7.en: **Grid System based on Fibonacci Spiral & Golden Rectangle**

sec-mark-notes/cell8.en: Visible in the artwork as construction lines, and they are part of the drawing, not scaffolding to be cleaned off. They are also the first thing to disappear as the file gets smaller — by 32 px they are grey haze (@fig-mark-sizes)

sec-mark-notes/cell10.en: The same direction and angle as the Leonardo hatch already running across the Tribute ground (`base.css`, `.hatch`) — an agreement nobody arranged, and worth keeping

sec-mark-notes/cell11.en: **Subtle texture / Enhances depth and form / Not overpowering**

sec-mark-notes/cell12.en: True at the sizes the sheet is drawn for. At 32 px the hatching has become tone rather than texture, and at 16 px it is a smudge. Nothing in the build can fix that; it is stated instead (@sec-mark-issues)

sec-mark-notes/cell14.en: Was `--field`, exactly, until 20 September 2026. The wall is now a darker, less saturated cut of it — the prototype's lightness at 21 % less chroma — because it went from a margin to the whole page (@sec-wall). This value remains the brand's: the mark, the icons and print use it

sec-mark-notes/cell16.en: **Not adopted as a site colour.** The site's ink and bar are `#3A2B22`, a warm brown the whole palette is solved against; a cool near-black beside sage reads as a second, colder identity. It is kept for print, where it is what the sheet says

sec-mark-notes/cell18.en: The variation that would suit the masthead best — and it is a *different drawing* from the preferred one: solid letters, no construction lines. It is still not used, because it is supplied at about 110 px. What the masthead carries since 20 September 2026 is the same idea arrived at from the preferred option: the drawing reduced to one colour and traced (@sec-mark-vector), set in cream on the bar. Reversed, from her own artwork

sec-mark-notes/cell20.en: Held in reserve for single-ink reproduction, where the hatching and the letter cannot be separated by lightness at all

sec-mark-notes/cell22.en: Was `--field-deep`, exactly, and moved with it (@sec-wall); still the sheet's, and still what the mark is drawn against

sec-mark-notes/cell24.en: **Not added.** It was within one step of what was then `--wash-blue` `#E9E3D6`, and a fifth cream is a fifth cream. The reading grounds have since gone sage and the creams with them; the artwork's own paper measures `#E4DCCC` and is kept as it is

sec-mark-notes/cell26.en: The icon build uses the sheet's clear-space rule as its crop, at 5.5 % of the monogram's side. The minimum size is the sheet's for print; the screen equivalents are in @sec-mark-issues, and they are smaller than 15 mm

sec-mark-notes/cell28.en: Both are on the sheet and neither is used yet. The site's masthead is its own lockup — the mark beside a wordmark already set in Fraunces — and the two supplied lockups set the name in a different face

sec-mark-notes/cell30.en: A line, not a tagline in use. It is not on the site, and nothing here proposes putting it there

sec-mark-notes/cell32.en: The sheet's own note on intent. Recorded, and it is the right description

sec-mark-issues/para1.en:
Four of these are worth more than a table row. None is a reason not to use the
artwork; all four are reasons to know what using it costs.

sec-mark-issues/para2.en:
**1 — There is no vector, and the raster is 1536 × 1024.** That is the whole
supply. The monogram occupies about 590 px of it, which is enough for a 180 px
home-screen icon and a masthead mark at 2× on a phone, and is the ceiling. A
business card, a 15 mm foil stamp or a gallery window would each want the
original vector or a much larger scan. **Ask for the source file** — it exists
somewhere, and it costs nothing to keep with the rest.

sec-mark-issues/para3.en:
**2 — A drawn mark does not survive 16 px.** @fig-mark-sizes shows the same
crop of the same file at each size that ships. At 180 px it is the drawing; at
32 px the construction lines have gone to haze and the hatching to tone; at
16 px what is left is a shape that reads as *a monogram* rather than as an S
and a C. That is the size a browser tab uses on a standard display. The
sheet's own answer to this is on the sheet — the **Monochrome** and
**Reversed** variations (@fig-mark-variations), which are solid-lettered
drawings without construction lines and would hold at 16 px. Switching the
small sizes to one of them is a one-line change in `scripts/build-icons.py`;
it is not made here, because the instruction was to use the preferred option
as it is.

sec-mark-issues/caption1.en: The variations panel, enlarged from @fig-brand. These are a *different drawing* from the preferred option — solid letters, no construction lines — and they are what the sheet offers for the sizes and grounds the preferred one cannot hold.

sec-mark-issues/para4.en:
**3 — The mark is a photograph of paper, not a shape.** It cannot take
`currentColor`, cannot invert for a dark theme, cannot be recoloured for a
seasonal card, and cannot be knocked out of a coloured ground. The site works
with that rather than against it: the artwork is opaque cream, so on the dark
masthead it arrived as a small mounted plate — a cream sheet on a dark ground,
which is the site's central visual idea at wordmark size. **There is a shape
too**, traced from the drawing for the surfaces that cannot hold a photograph;
what that costs is @sec-mark-vector. The masthead is one of them by Priscilla's
decision: the bar carries the vector, in the wordmark's own colour.

sec-mark-issues/para5.en:
**4 — The SVG favicon went away with it, and has come back.** The site once
shipped an `icon.svg`; a vector favicon is sharp at every size and is what a
tab would rather have. It was dropped because there was no vector of this mark
to ship, and an SVG wrapping a raster would be the same pixels behind a
vector's promise. That is the one issue here now closed rather than stated:
the tab is served a real shape again (@sec-mark-vector), with the 32 px PNG,
the `.ico`, the 180 px home-screen icon and the manifest behind it, all still
cut from the artwork by the icon build.

sec-mark-issues/caption2.en: The adopted artwork at the three sizes the build cuts, each enlarged from the file that actually ships.

sec-mark-vector/para1.en:
Issues 3 and 4 above are one missing object. A mark that cannot take a colour
cannot sit on a ground the site has not already decided, and a tab cannot be
given a drawing; both want a **shape**. There is no vector source — open item
7 — so one was made from the artwork, and this section is what it costs, since
a derivative that does not say what it is, is how a brand loses its own
artwork.

sec-mark-vector/para2.en:
**Why a threshold does not do it.** The letters in the drawing are not solid:
they are built from hatching, at about a 3 px pitch in a 592 px monogram. At
any single threshold a stroke therefore comes out striped, and morphology
wide enough to close the stripes is also wide enough to close the counters.
What *is* solid is the hatching's **density**, so the ink is blurred at a
little over the hatch's own pitch first, and the letters are the region where
that density stands above a level:

sec-mark-vector/tblcap1.en: The reduction, and what each number was solved against

sec-mark-vector/cell6.en: The sheet, rather than the brightest pixel: a specular fleck would otherwise set the white point

sec-mark-vector/cell9.en: A shade over the hatch's pitch. Under it the stripes survive as ripples in the outline — at 0.34 % the trace needs eight more curves and leaves a notch in the S's counter, where the ribbon's lit side falls under the level. Far over it, the thin joins of the S melt into the counter

sec-mark-vector/cell12.en: Where the C's left arm arrives whole without the construction lines arriving with it. By 0.34 the arm starts to break; under 0.18 the sheet's own construction circle is inside the letter

sec-mark-vector/cell15.en: Closes what the hatch left open, then takes off the ticks and the paper grain. Pockets the hatching left *inside* a stroke are filled: they are not counters, they are places where the drawing is pale

sec-mark-vector/cell18.en: The boundary is walked on the pixel lattice with the ink kept on the left, smoothed out of its staircase by four 1–2–1 passes, simplified at 1 px, and fitted with cubics to 1.2 px

sec-mark-vector/caption1.en: The reduction, stage by stage, and what it is for. Top: the drawing as supplied; its ink blurred at 0.5 % of the crop's side, which turns hatching into tone; the letters that stand above 0.22 of that tone's maximum; and the single path fitted to their boundary. Bottom: the same path on the wall, reversed on the bar and on the mat — it is one colour, so it is whatever colour it is set in — each with the 32 px and 16 px renderings enlarged beside it. Drawn by `docs/report/figures.py` from `scripts/build-mark-vector.py` itself, so the figure cannot describe a derivation the build does not perform.

sec-mark-vector/para3.en:
The result is **one closed path, 64 curves, 2.9 KB**, and it is measured
rather than admired: the builder renders its own output back to pixels and
reports the intersection-over-union against the reduction it came from, which
is **0.974**. `npm run check` re-runs the entire derivation and compares the
committed file byte for byte, so the vector cannot quietly become something
somebody edited by hand.

sec-mark-vector/para4.en:
**What the reduction cannot recover is which stroke passes in front.** In the
drawing the S crosses the C and is told apart from it by tone and by a drawn
outline. One colour has neither, so the two letters fuse where they cross.
Three ways to put the interlock back were tried and none survived being
looked at: the light *valley* between the strokes cuts into the lit side of
the S's own ribbon rather than between the letters; separating the dark cores
never yields two components, because at every threshold that keeps the letters
whole the strokes stay connected; and the drawing's own outline, which a ridge
filter does recover, cuts cleanly in two places out of four, which reads as
damage rather than as an interlock.

sec-mark-vector/para5.en:
The sheet's answer to this is a **different drawing** — the Monochrome and
Reversed variations (@fig-mark-variations), which resolve the overlap by hand
— and they are supplied at about 110 px, which is not enough to trace. So the
fused silhouette is what ships, and open item 7 gains its second reason: the
vector source would settle the interlock as well as the resolution.

sec-mark-vector/para6.en:
**Where it is used, and where it is not.** The tab, in both themes: `icon.svg`
carries the site's `--bar` for a light tab strip and its `--paper` for a dark
one, because a favicon has no page to inherit a colour from. Beside it,
`mark-sc.svg` carries no colour at all — inlined in a page it is whatever the
text around it is, and handed to a printer it is a shape rather than a
photograph of one.

sec-mark-vector/para7.en: And the **masthead**, which this section was written to leave open and which Priscilla decided. The bar carried the artwork itself, a cream plate of paper on the brown. What a photograph cannot do is take a colour: the mark could not follow the bar, could not invert, and carried a cream rectangle into a place where nothing else on the site has an edge. The vector can — it is one path in `currentColor`, inlined rather than linked because `currentColor` is a cascade and an `` has none, so the mark *is* the wordmark's colour and inherits every future change to it for nothing.

sec-mark-vector/para8.en:
Three things went with that change, and each is the same sentence: it is made
of ink now rather than of paper. The plate went — the radius and the mount
shadow said "a cream sheet lies on the bar", and there is no sheet. The size
came down from 2.1 em to 1.7 em, because the drawing needed the extra size to
hold its construction lines at 34 px and the traced shape has none. And the
cream is `--paper` at 11.45:1 on the bar, which is the wordmark's own colour
and the most legible pair on the site.

sec-mark-vector/para9.en:
Four assertions, F-05: that the committed vector re-derives from the pinned
artwork exactly, at an IoU of at least 0.95; that the inlinable copy names no
colour at all while the tab copy names the site's own two; that the SVG icon
is offered first with the raster set behind it, identically in both locales;
and that both files are stamped with the source and its hash, that nothing is
written back into `brand/`, and that this section still states what the
reduction costs.

sec-mark-construction/head.en: What was built before the artwork arrived

sec-mark-construction/para1.en:
This is kept on the record, not as a second live logo. Between the decision to
use a monogram and the arrival of the drawing, the site carried an `SC`
**constructed** from Fraunces — the face the wordmark is already set in — with
the outlines cut from the font at `opsz 40`, `wght 700` by
`scripts/build-mark-paths.py`. `scripts/mark.mjs` still holds it, and the build
asserts that nothing the *site* builds imports it: it exists so that @fig-mark-construction
can be drawn, and for no other reason.

sec-mark-construction/para2.en: Two things it settled are still worth having.

sec-mark-construction/para3.en:
The first is a **proportion**. Drawn at the sheet's literal 1 : 1.618 in a
square field, Fraunces' S falls to about the C's x-height and stops reading as
a capital — the mark reads *sC* — and the C's lower arm cannot reach far enough
left to close the hole the small S leaves. The construction used
1 : $\sqrt{\varphi}$ = 1 : 1.272 instead, the same construction one step in. It
is not a correction to the sheet: measured off Priscilla's own drawing, her S
is nearer 1 : 1.3 of her C than 1 : 1.618, so what the reconstruction found was
that the *stated* ratio and the *drawn* ratio are not the same number. The
drawn one is the one that reads.

sec-mark-construction/para4.en:
The second is the **size rule**: hatching comes off below about 96 px, because
below that it fills in. The construction could obey it, by simply not drawing
the hatch at small sizes. The artwork cannot, because the hatching is in the
pixels — which is issue 2 above, arrived at twice from opposite directions.

sec-mark-construction/caption1.en: The interim construction: an `SC` cut from Fraunces outlines, in the four renderings the sheet's variation set asks for, and at the three sizes that decide whether a mark works. Superseded by the artwork; kept because the size argument survived it.

sec-mark-not/head.en: What it deliberately does not do

sec-mark-not/item1.en: **It spends no accent.** Sanguine is reserved for calls to action. Nothing in the artwork is sanguine, and nothing has been tinted to make it so.

sec-mark-not/item2.en: **It has no per-locale variant**, by construction, for the reason in @sec-mark-constraint: the same file, byte for byte, on both homepages.

sec-mark-not/item3.en: **It contributes no accessible name.** In the masthead the mark is an `` with an *empty* `alt` inside the wordmark link, so the link's name is the gallery's name and nothing else — 2.5.3 Label in Name, and 2.4.4.

sec-mark-not/item4.en: **It is not cleaned up.** No tracing, no background removal, no contrast boost, no redrawing of the construction lines. `scripts/build-icons.py` is asserted to do nothing but crop, resize and save. The vector in @sec-mark-vector does trace — that is what it is for — but it is a second, declared object beside the artwork rather than a tidied version of it: the original is untouched, still pinned by hash, and still what the masthead and every raster icon are cut from.

sec-mark-where/para1.en:
The icon set — `icon-32.png`, `favicon.ico`, the 180 px home-screen icon and
the manifest; `logo-mark.png` in the masthead, where the mark and the name are
a single link and a single tab stop; and this document, in the footer of every
page — all from `brand/mark-lockup.png`, by one crop, except the masthead,
which since 20 September 2026 carries the vector instead. From the same crop
by way of the reduction in @sec-mark-vector: `icon.svg`, which the tab is
offered first, `mark-sc.svg`, which carries no colour and is there for
anything that has to supply its own, and the path inlined into the bar.

sec-mark-where/para2.en:
The sheet's **horizontal lockup** was tried on this document's title page and
taken off again, which is worth recording because it puts a number on open
item 7. The lockup is **279 px** wide in the supply. At the 52 mm a title page
wants it, that is **136 dpi**, and its wordmark's capitals are about 2 mm tall —
type at 136 dpi is visibly soft in print, and this report is going to be
printed properly. The monogram survives the same test easily (256 px at 8.8 mm
is 738 dpi) and Fraunces is an outline at any size, so the title page carries
the monogram with the name set beside it, exactly as the site's masthead does.
Nothing about that is a preference; it is the resolution ceiling, met.

sec-mark-where/para3.en:
Thirteen assertions in `scripts/check-review.mjs` (F-01 to F-05) hold it together:
that both originals are present and byte-for-byte the files that were supplied;
that every derivative is a crop and a resize of the lockup and of nothing else,
with no drawing, tracing or recolouring in the builder; that the masthead
carries the artwork at a declared size and mounted as a plate; that the mark
takes no accessible name of its own and is identical in both locales; that
nothing the site builds redraws it; that the costs in @sec-mark-issues are
still stated rather than quietly absorbed; and that this section still quotes
the sheet's own values rather than paraphrasing them; and that the vector
re-derives from the artwork exactly, names no colour of its own, and says in
its own file what it came from.

sec-soft/para1.en:
The site as first built was correct and a little hard: square sheet, flat
works, a colour swap for a hover and hard stops where sections met. This pass
asked for something softer and more elegant — without making it less
professional, and without changing a single colour.

sec-soft/para2.en:
Those two constraints do most of the design work. Every familiar softening
technique reaches for new colour (a white card, a black shadow, a coloured
glow) or for lower contrast (translucency), and this site has already argued,
with measurements, against both.

sec-soft-limits/para1.en:
Three commitments made earlier in this document bound what "soft" may mean
here.

sec-soft-limits/item1.en: **Quietness is bought with size and whitespace, never with contrast.** Anything translucent puts text over a ground that is no longer a token, so its contrast has to be measured against the worst thing that can pass beneath it — which, on a site of paintings, is white.

sec-soft-limits/item2.en: **Edges dissolve rather than rule** (@sec-masters). A softer site should have *fewer* lines, not decorative new ones.

sec-soft-limits/item3.en: **A painting is never altered.** Rounding its corner crops it. Zooming it on hover implies it was cropped to fit. Stretching it misrepresents the object for sale.

sec-soft-limits/para2.en:
Motion has its own limit, already recorded in the stylesheet: many
viewport-heights of large images make scroll-triggered movement a vestibular
risk, and every animation must stand down when the reader has asked for
reduced motion.

sec-soft-research/caption1.en: Left: how translucent the masthead may be, measured as navigation text over a white passage of a painting. Right: the lightness of a section boundary from top to bottom, before and after — and, dashed, the profile the same rule draws when the plates are painted, since with them off (@sec-plates) a boundary is flat. Both panels are computed from the live token file.

sec-soft-research/para1.en:
**Glass has a hard floor, and it is high.** The usual glassmorphism panel runs
at 60–70% opacity. Over a white passage that puts the navigation at
3.06–4.11:1: a failure at caption size. WCAG's 4.5:1 is reached at 73%; a full
AAA margin of 7:1 needs 87%. The glass that is legal here is subtle by
necessity, and the right-hand side of @fig-softness is why it is still worth
having: a painting passing under a solid bar is cut off by a slab, while under
88% it is *felt* as a soft blur of its own colour.

sec-soft-research/para2.en:
**Glass at rest would repaint the brand.** Prototyping showed a problem no
contrast figure reveals: a translucent bar at the top of the page sits over the
sage, so every page would show a greyed, greenish masthead instead of
Priscilla's brown. Glass is only wanted once there is something beneath it.

sec-soft-research/para3.en:
**A boundary between near-identical washes is invisible and hard at once.** The
washes differ by ΔE 0.8–2.6 in OKLab — at or under the threshold of perception
when spread across 9 rem — so a boundary is only ever seen where it breaks: a
band that fades to the wrong neighbour, or a section with no band at all, leaves
a hard step that reads as a faint line. A band must fade between the grounds
actually either side of it, and be visible enough to be felt.

sec-soft-research/para4.en:
**A peak reads as a crease.** A boundary that rises and falls through a few
evenly weighted stops draws a pointed profile, and the eye finds the point. The
adopted band follows a raised cosine across nine stops, which is what the
right-hand panel of @fig-softness plots — read back out of the stylesheet rather
than redrawn. The nine stops are still in the rule; the curve is drawn dashed
there because `--edge-breath` is currently 0% (@sec-plates) and the band it
draws is flat.

sec-soft-research/para5.en:
**Motion on this site must settle, not perform.** The motion tokens already
say *leave quickly, settle slowly, never overshoot*. Cross-document view
transitions let a painting carry from the list into its own page. They need a
unique name per element on each page; two elements sharing a name abort the
whole transition, which rules out naming the lightbox copy.

sec-soft-options/para1.en:
Every option considered is listed. **Adopted** items are built. **Optional**
items remain available for a later pass, and where one fails a measured limit
the reason says so.

sec-soft-options/cell6.en: 2 px on controls and panels, 3 px on the sheet

sec-soft-options/cell8.en: Softens the pixel-hard corner without changing shape; a mount board is square

sec-soft-options/cell12.en: Reads as an app, not a gallery

sec-soft-options/cell16.en: Rounding a corner removes part of the object being sold

sec-soft-options/cell20.en: A brown shadow sits *in* the paper; a black one sits on it and reads grey

sec-soft-options/cell28.en: What a gallery does to a work; defined by tone and shadow, not a line

sec-soft-options/cell32.en: Crisper and more card-like, but adds the line the site avoids

sec-soft-options/cell36.en: Softer still; loses the mounted look

sec-soft-options/cell38.en: Sheet floating from 900 px, not 1320 px

sec-soft-options/cell40.en: On a 1280 px laptop the sheet used to run into the bar

sec-soft-options/cell44.en: 7.39:1 over white; solid at rest; nothing passes under it on a phone

sec-soft-options/cell50.en: Translucent reading panels over the sage

sec-soft-options/cell52.en: The sheet is the reading surface; text on glass over a painting has no worst case to solve against

sec-soft-options/cell56.en: Behind it is the sage, not a painting, so the worst case is one computable colour: 9.13:1

sec-soft-options/cell58.en: Frosted plates on the sheet, at 72%

sec-soft-options/cell60.en: Cream over cream: the composite is always lighter than the wash beneath, so it cannot make any text worse

sec-soft-options/cell62.en: A fall from a lifted `--field` to `--field-deep`

sec-soft-options/cell64.en: The largest solid on the site, and the only surface with nothing happening in it. Carries no text at any width

sec-soft-options/cell66.en: The field breathing through each band at 20%

sec-soft-options/cell68.en: ΔE 5.3: plainly there when scrolling, a fifth of the way to the sage

sec-soft-options/cell70.en: Bands named by, and fading between, their actual neighbours

sec-soft-options/cell72.en: No hard step where a band meets the section beside it

sec-soft-options/cell74.en: Each section its own sheet, with sage between

sec-soft-options/cell76.en: The most emphatic; replaces one mounted sheet with several and doubles the shadows

sec-soft-options/cell78.en: The mark set small at the centre of a band

sec-soft-options/cell80.en: A signpost that repeats the logo on every scroll

sec-soft-options/cell82.en: A hairline or short sanguine rule

sec-soft-options/cell83.en: Optional — *adds a line and spends the accent*

sec-soft-options/cell86.en: Nav underline drawn in from the left

sec-soft-options/cell88.en: A transform, so nothing reflows and the 48 px target is unchanged

sec-soft-options/cell90.en: One-pixel button lift, pointer devices only

sec-soft-options/cell92.en: On touch, `:hover` sticks after a tap

sec-soft-options/cell94.en: Mount shadow deepens when a work is hovered

sec-soft-options/cell100.en: No scale: a painting drawn at 99.5% is drawn wrong

sec-soft-options/cell104.en: Implies cropping; no hover on touch

sec-soft-options/cell108.en: Also invisible in a link-card thumbnail and the first frame

sec-soft-options/cell112.en: A focus indicator must be present the instant focus arrives

sec-soft-options/cell114.en: Masthead held still across page changes

sec-soft-options/cell116.en: Without it the whole bar dissolves and re-forms, which reads as a reload

sec-soft-options/cell118.en: The painting carried from list to page

sec-soft-options/cell120.en: Chromium and Safari; elsewhere navigation is simply instant

sec-soft-options/cell124.en: A long glide past many large images; already declined

sec-soft-built/caption1.en: The adopted treatment, with a synthetic stand-in canvas in place of photography that does not exist yet. Left: hover — the navigation underline drawn, the mount lifted, the button raised one pixel. Top right: the glass bar at its scrolled state, with the canvas's near-white highlight beneath it. Bottom right: the homepage boundary between Latest works and Series, which with the plates off (@sec-plates) is now flat sage: the mat, the shadows and the glass are what the pass left behind, and the band is what it took away.

sec-soft-built/para1.en:
Nothing in the palette changed. Every softness token — two radii, three
shadows, the mat, the glass values and the boundary breath — is expressed
through colours that already existed, and a check fails the build if a literal
colour appears among them.

sec-soft-glass/para1.en:
A second pass on 18 September took the same treatment to the three surfaces the
first one left flat, on the same terms: **nothing is translucent over a ground
whose colour cannot be named.**

sec-soft-glass/item1.en: **The field.** The sage ran as one fill from edge to edge — the largest solid on the site. It keeps its colour and gains a slow fall from a lifted `--field` at the top to `--field-deep` at the foot, fixed rather than scrolling, so the sheet reads as mounted on a ground that is lit. Both ends are palette values, and no text sits on the field at any width, so none of it is a contrast question.

sec-soft-glass/item2.en: **The footer.** It runs the bar's own glass at 88%. Where the masthead's worst case has to be *assumed* — a painting can put pure white under it — the footer's is a single computable colour, because what is behind it is the field. That composite is written down as `--glass-footer` `#43372C`, and `check-contrast.mjs` recomputes it from `--bar`, `--glass-bar-opacity` and `--field` on every run and fails on any drift. Footer text measures **9.13:1** on it, and the contact details EU and Chinese law require to be published are the text in question.

sec-soft-glass/item3.en: **Plates on the sheet.** The contact panel is now a frosted plate rather than a second ground stamped on the first. The safety argument is arithmetic: `--wash-lift` is lighter than every reading ground, so 72% of it over `--wash-deep` — the darkest of the three — composites to `#EBEFDD`, *lighter* than `--wash-deep`. A plate can only make the ground under text paler than the one already solved against, never darker. Since the plates came off the ground beneath it is the field (@sec-plates), and the same arithmetic now works the other way round: the panel is the one surface on the site that lifts its text back over 4.5:1.

sec-soft-glass/para2.en:
So that a rule can say what it is really read on, a stylesheet rule may now
declare a `--contrast-ground`. The check prefers it over whatever background
the rule also paints, which is how a surface painted in a `color-mix()` the
script cannot composite still gets solved against a real colour. The footer,
the legal declaration and the channel row all declare one.

sec-soft-line/head.en: The line that says a section ended

sec-soft-line/para1.en:
The sfumato bands were built to dissolve a boundary rather than rule it, and
they do — while there is something either side to dissolve. With the plates
off there is not: a band joins the wall to the wall, `--edge-breath` is 0, and
all four paint nothing at all (@sec-plates). What that left was nine rem of
spacing between sections and a page that read as one long scroll.

sec-soft-line/para2.en:
So a boundary is now **stated**: an engraved hairline at the centre of each
band — one line of shade with one line of light caught under it, 2 px in all.
It is the pair an emboss is made of, and it is not a colour: black and white
at low alpha, so the same two tokens work over the wall, over the About panel
and over anything either of them is later changed to. The About panel's
outline is the same pair, which is the point of there being only two — the
page has one idea of what an edge is rather than a hairline here and a border
there.

sec-soft-line/para3.en:
It is drawn on a pseudo-element rather than folded into the gradient, so the
two mechanisms stay independent: restore the plates and `--edge-breath` and
the sfumato returns *underneath* the line, not instead of it. N-02 asserts
that both — the boundaries and the panel — are drawn from that one pair, and
that nothing else in the stylesheet uses it.

sec-soft-canvas/para1.en:
The brief for this pass was the texture in the artwork, and not one colour with
it. So the texture was **measured off the artwork** rather than chosen: a
300 px patch of blank ground in `brand/mark-lockup.png` has a mean of `#E4DCCC`
and a luminance standard deviation of **4.87 of 255**, about 2.2 %, and its
spatial spectrum falls off as 1/f with no periodic peak. That last detail
settles what it is. A woven canvas has a weave, and a weave shows as a peak;
this is a **cold-press cotton-rag sheet** — paper fibre, not cloth. What the
