tile ended up on is a mat board, which is the same material by another name.

sec-soft-canvas/para2.en:
One tile in `tokens.css` reproduces it: `feTurbulence`, desaturated, its output
compressed to a narrow band about 0.5, tiled at 400 px. Getting the *character*
right took as much measuring as getting the amplitude right — the first tile
matched σ almost exactly and still read as a fine woven mesh rather than as
paper, because a high octave count on an anisotropic base frequency makes
`feTurbulence`'s own lattice visible. Six candidates were rendered beside a 1:1
crop of the artwork and compared; what the paper has is broad, cloudy
low-frequency mottle with a faint tooth over it, which is a low base frequency
and many octaves. Measured back out of Chrome on the built page, the field
reads at **σ 4.77** against the artwork's 4.87.

sec-soft-canvas/callout1.en: Why it cannot change a colour, and why that needed measuring

sec-soft-canvas/para3.en:
The tile is neutral grey with a mean of exactly 0.5, and it is composited in
`soft-light`. Soft-light with a 0.5 source is the **identity** —
$B(C_b, 0.5) = C_b$ — so the mean of a textured surface is the token it was
painted with, and the grain only modulates around it. Measured, the largest
mean drift on any ground is **0.9 of 255**, or 0.35 %.

sec-soft-canvas/para4.en:
That is true only because the filter declares
`color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"`. Without it SVG filters run in linearRGB,
`feTurbulence`'s 0.5 mean arrives as **0.73** in sRGB, and the tile that was
supposed to be an identity lightens everything it touches. The first render
did exactly that, and it was caught by measuring the result rather than by
reading the specification — which is the same lesson as @sec-trap, in a
different currency.

sec-soft-canvas/para5.en:
**Where it may go** was decided twice, and the second answer is the short one:
**one material.** The tile is on the mat around a painting and on nothing else.

sec-soft-canvas/para6.en:
It was on three things — the field, the bands between sections, and the mat —
and both of the others came off on 20 September 2026, each for its own reason
and neither of them a matter of taste.

sec-soft-canvas/para7.en:
The **field** came off because it is the largest surface on the site, which
made the grain most of what you saw rather than something you found. Nothing
was lost in colour: the tile is mean-neutral under soft-light, so the field was
never anything but `--field` either way. The brief for it was one line —
*revert the sage backgrounds to the uncanvassed version, as in the original
prototype* — and that is what the field is now: her flat green, lit from a
raised `--field` at the top to `--field-deep` at the foot.

sec-soft-canvas/para8.en:
The **bands** came off because the reason they had it turned out not to be
true. A band carried the same tile at 30 % as a *dither*, on the assumption
that a nine-rem fade in eight bits must step visibly. Measured at 1× over the
built page, with the intended ramp subtracted so that only the error remains:

sec-soft-canvas/tblcap1.en: What the dither was actually doing to a section boundary

sec-soft-canvas/para9.en:
Banding is a *horizontal stripe*, so the row-mean residual is the thing that
measures it — and it is **lower without the tile than with it**. The browser
dithers the gradient itself; the tile was adding per-pixel noise and no
smoothness. The band's whole range is 19 of 255 over 144 px, about 21 levels,
so even an engine that does not dither steps one level at a time across seven
rows.

sec-soft-canvas/para10.en:
What is left is a rule about material rather than about arithmetic, and that
is a change worth naming. The arithmetic used to bind: `check-contrast.mjs`
solves how far a mean-neutral grain could move each reading ground before its
tightest pair fell through its floor, and on cream the answer was nearly
nothing. On the sage grounds it is no longer the constraint —

sec-soft-canvas/tblcap2.en: How much texture each reading ground could take

sec-soft-canvas/para11.en:
— the palest reading ground could now carry the whole tile and be measurably
fine. It does not get it, because it is a wall and not a board. The check still
fails the build if any rule ever paints a reading ground *and* textures it, and
`check-review.mjs` G-07 asserts the narrower rule by name: the textured
selectors are the mat and the video's mat, and there are two of them.

sec-soft-canvas/para12.en:
**This document is no longer printed on it.** Every page of this report used to
be `--wash-warm` carrying the same tile, on the argument that it was the site's
own paper. The site's paper is untextured now, so the argument has expired: the
report is printed on `--wash-pale`, flat. It also removes a 300 dpi image from
underneath every page, which is one less thing between the press and the type.

sec-soft-canvas/para13.en:
The page you are holding therefore carries a colour the site itself no longer
paints (@sec-plates), and keeps it deliberately. A screen is lit and a page is
not; a printed page has no field behind it to show through, and every word of
this document is a word that has to be read. `--wash-pale` is the lightest
ground the project ever solved for prose, which is the right paper for a
document whichever way the site's own switch is set.

sec-soft-held/item1.en: `check-contrast.mjs` composites the bar at `--glass-bar-opacity` over pure white and fails the build below 7:1 for navigation text. Set to the usual 70%, it names three failures.

sec-soft-held/item2.en: `check-render.mjs` lays the built pages out in Chrome and asserts that every painting's box keeps the painting's own proportions to within 1%, with no radius and no transform (@sec-checks).

sec-soft-held/item3.en: Three more (G-07) cover the canvas: one tile, defined once and referenced exactly twice; the tile neutral, symmetric about 0.5, declared in sRGB and blended with soft-light; and the textured selectors exactly the two mats.

sec-soft-held/item4.en: Five more (L-01 to L-05) cover the decisions of 20 September 2026: the fifteen rules allowed to paint cream and no sixteenth; the three reading grounds all at the field's own hue and all above the lightness where `--muted-ui` fails; the italic a real file with synthesis off; About set as a book page in both languages, including the two refusals on the Chinese one; and every surface that is read painting a plate token, with no rule naming a wash directly, so that the plates stay reversible from the token file alone (@sec-plates).

sec-soft-held/item5.en: Six assertions in `check-review.mjs` (G-01 to G-06) cover the rest: no literal colour in the new tokens — with one named exception, `--glass-footer`, allowed only while the contrast check recomputes it — a mat and nothing that alters a painting, glass solid at rest and gated, all new motion standing down for reduced motion, one transition name per painting per page, and every band joining the grounds actually either side of it — by their plate tokens, so the join holds whatever those plates are painted.

sec-masters/para1.en:
The brief asked for a debt to Leonardo\index{Leonardo da Vinci} and to van Gogh\index{van Gogh, Vincent}, carried without ever
announcing itself. The test applied throughout: *a visitor who knows nothing
should feel only that the site is calm and well made; a visitor who knows the
work should feel recognised.*

what-was-adopted/item1.en: **The accent is sanguine**\index{sanguine}. Red chalk, the medium Leonardo drew in, measures 6.33:1 on white; the oxblood Priscilla chose by eye measures 6.68:1. They are the same colour. The recommendation was to change nothing and record why.

what-was-adopted/item2.en: **No hard edges.** Leonardo's instruction to paint *"without strokes or lines, in the manner of smoke"*\index{sfumato} and the Chinese 没骨 ("boneless") tradition of painting without contour are the same idea reached independently. For a Chinese painter addressing both audiences that is a structural principle, not a motif. Section boundaries dissolve rather than rule.

what-was-adopted/item3.en: **The rules are van Gogh's stated violet.** He told Theo the *Bedroom* walls were "of a pale violet"; they read blue today because the red lake faded. The site uses the colour he said, not the colour that survived.

what-was-adopted/item4.en: **Hatching runs his way.** Leonardo was left-handed, so his stroke runs upper-left to lower-right. No text source could be retrieved, so the 43.8° angle is an original structure-tensor measurement of his sheets, validated against a right-handed control.

sec-cut/para1.en:
**Golden-ratio grid.** Unsupported. Illustrating Pacioli's *De divina
proportione* establishes that Leonardo drew the solids, not that he composed on
the ratio.

sec-cut/para2.en:
**"Leonardo invented sfumato", and the word itself.** Cennino Cennini described
blending shadows like smoke a century earlier, and Leonardo never used the
noun — a full-text search of the *Trattato* returns none.

sec-cut/para3.en:
**Any yellow as text.** Indian yellow is 2.10:1 and zinc yellow 1.53:1. Both are
genuine *Starry Night* pigments and both are unusable for anything but a mark
inside an image.

sec-cut/para4.en:
**Sampling colours off the paintings.** The *Bedroom* wall as it survives today
is 2.78:1; the *Sunflowers* chrome yellow 2.70:1. Both sit within a hair of the
2.67:1 failure this report opens with.

sec-structure/para1.en:
The first build's menu — *Original Works, Tribute, About, How to Buy* — mixed
jumps down the homepage with real pages, had no page that listed the works, and
could group a work only by a two-value field. None of that survives a catalogue
growing past a few dozen works, or a new genre. The structure below replaced it.

sec-structure-method/para1.en:
Six reference sites, chosen to cover the three models this site sits between:
artists' own sites (David Hockney, Kehinde Wiley Studio), galleries (David
Zwirner, Victoria Miro) and marketplaces for original work (Saatchi Art,
Artfinder). Each was **rendered in headless Chrome**, not fetched as HTML: two
of the six build their navigation and filters with scripts, and a plain fetch
reported Saatchi as having no filters at all. Navigation, hierarchy, breadcrumbs
and side columns were read from the rendered page and checked against a
screenshot. Three first choices could not be used: Gerhard Richter's site was
offline, Hauser & Wirth rate-limited the request, and Artsy refused it.

sec-structure-method/para2.en:
Counting `<aside>` elements suggested four of the six had sidebars; every one
was a region-settings pop-up, so only the rendered layout was trusted.

sec-structure-consensus/para1.en:
Columns: **H** Hockney · **W** Kehinde Wiley · **Z** David Zwirner · **VM** Victoria Miro ·
**S** Saatchi Art · **A** Artfinder.

sec-structure-consensus/cell9.en: Works under one entry; no series beside About

sec-structure-consensus/cell41.en: Highlights or latest in a sidebar

sec-structure-consensus/cell65.en: *How to buy* as a header page

sec-structure-consensus/para2.en:
Two things the table does not show. The filter sidebars both belong to
marketplaces listing tens of thousands of works — Artfinder's showed *60 of
25,000*. And where an artist's own site organises a large body of work, it does
it one level down: Hockney's *Works* opens onto media, and within *Paintings* a
horizontal row of decades.

sec-structure-sidebar/para1.en: No. Not for navigation, highlights or anything latest.

sec-structure-sidebar/item1.en: **None of the six uses one for navigation or highlights.**

sec-structure-sidebar/item2.en: **Right-hand columns are not looked at.** Eye-tracking puts desktop attention on right-rail content at 0.8% of fixations: people have learned that the side column is where advertising lives, and avoid it whatever it holds.[^nng-rail]

sec-structure-sidebar/item3.en: **Local navigation is for large sections.** It earns its space when visitors browse and compare many sibling pages, and is not needed for small ones; when it is used it should be less prominent than the global navigation.[^nng-local]

sec-structure-sidebar/item4.en: **Filters belong beside the grid only when there are many of them.** Sidebar filters are often overlooked because they sit where navigation and banners usually are; a horizontal row above the results works for up to six to eight filter types, and a sidebar is the better choice beyond that.[^baymard-filters]

sec-structure-sidebar/para2.en:
Where this site needs what a sidebar would carry, it gets it in the reading
path instead: the *latest* works are a homepage section, each series is a room
with its own page, and the Works section's rooms are one quiet row of tabs.

sec-structure-built/caption1.en: The site map before and after. The after tree is drawn from `site.json`, the same data the build generates the navigation and series from.

sec-structure-built/item1.en: **The header goes to four real pages:** *Works, About, How to Buy, Contact* (作品, 关于, 购买方式, 联系), and marks the one the visitor is in — `page` on the section's own page, `true` beneath it.

sec-structure-built/item2.en: **Works is the catalogue.** `/works/` lists every available work, newest first, with a row of tabs: *All, Original Works, Tribute, Sold works*, each with its count. Each series is a room at `/works/series/{id}/`; sold works moved from `/archive/` to `/works/sold/`.

sec-structure-built/item3.en: **Series are data.** A series is one entry in `site.json`; its page, its tab and its homepage card are generated from it, and the build refuses a work that names an undeclared series or genre, or a slug that would collide with a page under `/works/`.

sec-structure-built/item4.en: **The homepage is a front door, not the catalogue:** van Gogh's line — his Dutch above the reader's language — beside one *Featured work*, the four *Latest works* with a link to all of them and their number, a card for each series, About, and How to Buy.

sec-structure-built/item5.en: **Breadcrumbs from the second level down,** with the current page as text and a work's trail running through its one series (*Home / Works / Tribute / …*), and published as structured data. The top level has none: there is nothing above it to return to.

sec-structure-built/item6.en: **The footer carries the channels as marks.** Instagram, Facebook, X, Bluesky, 小红书 and WeChat, drawn on one 24-unit grid at one stroke weight in the footer's own colour — a set that belongs to this site rather than six logo files that belong to six other companies. Each is a 48 px target with a visually hidden name, because an icon has no accessible name of its own. A handle turns its mark into the real profile link; WeChat and 小红书, which have no address derivable from a handle, go to the contact page where the handle is printed. **Until a channel has its handle its mark still appears and links to a route that does not exist,** so the click lands on the 404 page — the same arrangement decision D1 used for search, account and cart while those three had controls, and policed the same way: the route must be declared in `site.placeholders.social`, and must still be dead. Readiness rule ID-06 requires every channel to be a handle or an explicit `""` before a release will build, which is what clears the placeholders by itself.

sec-structure-built/item7.en: **Nothing that was shared breaks.** Work pages keep their addresses. `/archive/` answers with a 301 on Cloudflare Pages and with a redirecting page on hosts that cannot send one.

sec-structure-order/para1.en:
The site has four places to go — *Works, About, How to Buy, Contact* — and
Priscilla asked for them in that order, in the header and on the homepage.
The header was already in it. The question worth answering was whether it is
the right one, and what the homepage should do with it, so the sample from
@sec-structure-method was widened and read for **order** rather than for
structure.

sec-structure-order/tblcap1.en: What eight sites put first, and where they put Contact

sec-structure-order/cell6.en: Exhibitions · Artists · Fairs & Collecting · Quarterly · News · Locations · Shop

sec-structure-order/cell10.en: Artists · Exhibitions · Art Fairs · Events · Journal · Publishing · Galleries

sec-structure-order/cell14.en: Artists · Exhibitions · Art Fairs · Channel · Store

sec-structure-order/cell23.en: Collect · Artists · The Edits · Journal · Info · Gift Cards

sec-structure-order/cell27.en: New In · Painting · Prints · Photography · Sculpture · Drawing · Artists

sec-structure-order/cell31.en: Shop Art · Our Artists · Commissions · About Us

sec-structure-order/cell35.en: the catalogue, by medium and by artist

sec-structure-order/para2.en: Three things every one of them agrees on.

sec-structure-order/para3.en:
**The work is first.** Eight out of eight open with the catalogue under one
name or another — *Exhibitions, Artists, Collect, Shop Art, New In*. Not one
leads with the gallery's own story.

sec-structure-order/para4.en:
**Contact is last, or it is not in the header at all.** Six of the eight keep
it in the footer entirely; the two that surface it put it at the end. Nothing
in the sample puts Contact before About.

sec-structure-order/para5.en:
**Four to six items.** The marketplaces run longer because their nav *is* the
catalogue's facets; the artists' and galleries' own sites sit at four to six.
This site has four.

sec-structure-order/para6.en:
That settles the order by convention, and the **serial position effect**
settles why it is the right one rather than merely the common one: in any
list, the first and last items are the ones attended to and remembered, and
the middle is where attention goes to die.[^serial] The two that matter
commercially here are the first — the work, which is the product — and the
last — Contact, which on a site with no cart is the checkout. About and How to
Buy are the reasons to act, and they belong between the two.

sec-structure-order/para7.en:
Where this site departs from the sample, it does so knowingly, and both
departures come from the same fact: **there is no cart, and the border is in
the way**.

sec-structure-order/item1.en: **How to Buy is in the header.** Five of the eight keep buying help in the footer, behind an FAQ. Here, how buying works is a question the visitor has *before* they choose anything — payment is arranged by message, duty is the buyer's to anticipate, and the returns window is a promise that has to be found. The threshold for moving it to the footer is already written down (@tbl-structure-growth): when the cart takes payments.

sec-structure-order/item2.en: **About is in the header.** The galleries push their own story into the footer because the artists are the product. Here the artist *is* the product: the pledge, the slowness and the reason there are not many works are what a buyer is buying into.

sec-structure-order/para8.en:
**The homepage now runs in the same order**, and ends where the header ends.
It used to stop at *How to Buy*: it explained how buying works and handed the
reader to the footer, which is where a legal address lives rather than where
an invitation does. A **Contact close** was added — the section's own intro
and one quiet link, with the details left in the one place they already live —
so the last thing on the page is how to reach the person who painted it.

sec-structure-order/para9.en:
One link came off in the same pass. The band under the masthead carried a
*View works* link out of the hero with it (@sec-band); the header's first item
already goes there and the Latest works section ends with the same link, so a
third route to one page, inside the page's own statement, was a link asking to
be counted rather than used. The band is the quote and the palette now, and
nothing else. I-07 asserts the header's order and the page's, in both
languages.

sec-structure-personal/para1.en: The consensus decides the shape; the site keeps its own character inside it.

sec-structure-personal/item1.en: **Tribute keeps its room.** The van Gogh epigraph and the hatch texture that marked its homepage section now mark its series page — the room it belongs in — and it has a card of its own on the homepage.

sec-structure-personal/item2.en: **The front door keeps the gallery's voice:** the motto in two languages and one painting, and the sfumato bands between sections, each still joining the grounds either side of it.

sec-structure-personal/item3.en: **One departure from the six.** None of them puts *How to Buy* in the header, and here it stays there. The six either take cards through an ordinary checkout or sell to collectors who expect to enquire. This site sells across a border, without cards, with import duty the buyer has to anticipate, and with its cart still a placeholder; how buying works is a question a visitor has before they have chosen anything. When the cart works, *How to Buy* moves to the footer and the cart becomes the header's way in to buying — as five of the six have it.

sec-band/para1.en:
The gallery's own line — van Gogh's *wat met liefde gedaan wordt dat wordt
goed gedaan*, and its translation — used to stand in the hero's left column
beside the featured painting, with *View works* under it. Six words and a link
holding a column open next to an object is the arrangement finding A-01 was
about in the first place, one step further on: a quote that is the gallery's
statement is not a sibling of a work, it is the top of the page.

sec-band/para2.en:
It is now a **band**, full width, immediately under the masthead, held open by
its padding and closed by an engraved line. The hero below carries nothing but
the painting.

sec-band/para3.en:
It is **painted in the About panel's dark sage**, `#727A5C`. On the bare wall
it was a stretch of page with a quotation lying on it rather than a band, and
the boundary at its foot ruled one green off from the same green. Painted, the
two places this site speaks in the first person — the gallery's own line, and
the artist's own — share a ground, and the boundary has an edge to state.

sec-band/para4.en:
That ground is the exact centre of the mid-tone squeeze (@sec-panel): pure
black measures 4.65:1 on it and pure white 4.52, so the whole palette has about
3% of headroom and `--ink-deep` is the only token that clears 4.5. The Dutch,
the translation and the attribution were `--body`, `--ink` and `--muted`, which
measure 3.73, 4.33 and 3.50 on this green — all three under the floor — and are
now that one ink, exactly as everything in the About panel is. The hairline
between his words and their translation went with them: `--rule-soft` is solved
for the wall at 1.36:1 and measures 1.79 here, which is a line you read rather
than one you feel, so the band draws it in the wall's own colour, 1.34 on this
green. `check-contrast` solves the panel as a ground, so a fourth colour cannot
arrive here unmeasured.

sec-band/para5.en: Three things had to be measured rather than chosen.

sec-band/para6.en:
**The fold.** A band that pushes the painting off the opening screen would
undo A-01 with better manners. At 1440 × 900 the masthead is 110 px, the band
330, the hero's own padding came down from 96 to 48, and the featured
painting now starts at y = 600 in a release build — on screen, where the
finding asked for it.

sec-band/para7.en:
**The shape of the quote.** It was set in four short lines, so that the Dutch
and the English stood in the same shape; in a wide band four short lines are a
column, which is the thing the band exists to stop being. Both are now two
lines, still the same shape as each other, and still set as written.

sec-band/para8.en:
**The size at every width.** The motto may never be re-wrapped by the browser
— the attribution is aligned to the real right edge of its longest line, and a
browser cannot shrink a box to the longest line of wrapped text. So its size is
decided by that line rather than by taste: *"with love is well done."* is
10.42 ems wide, which is 563 px at the ladder's 54 px ceiling inside a 1060 px
column, and 271 px at its 26 px floor inside the 280 a 320 px screen gives.

sec-band/para9.en:
The `clamp()` of @sec-scale-fluid does that continuously, and for every heading rather than for the motto alone; two hand-set step-downs at 519 px and 359 px did it before. `check-render` measures the rendered line count against the `
`s at five widths either way and fails the build on a re-wrap.

sec-band/para10.en:
The band sits **between `<header>` and `<main>`** rather than inside either.
Inside the header it would become the sticky bar's containing block, and the
bar would stop sticking once the band scrolled past — which is the bar
@sec-soft-glass measures. Inside `main` it would be inside the mounted sheet,
and a band that stops at the mount's rounded corner is not a band. It carries
no landmark of its own, so the page's landmark count is what it was.

sec-band/para11.en:
**The band carries no ornament.** Four decorative rules in the sheet's own
brand colours were drawn across its foot and then taken out (@sec-review-aw):
on sage they read as a progress bar or a palette chip, and the cream one as a
stray highlight — the only unexplained mark on a site whose argument is that
nothing here is unexplained. `check-review` N-01 holds them out, of the markup
and of the stylesheet both.

sec-portrait/para1.en:
A site selling one painter's work had no photograph of the painter. About is
the one part of it that is a person rather than a catalogue — the pledge, the
reason there are not many works, the sentence about pausing in front of one —
and it was set as an essay with nobody in it.

sec-portrait/para2.en:
It is now framed in both the places About appears, and in both it sits at the
**foot of the prose**, in the same column, like a sign-off.

sec-portrait/para3.en:
Not at the head. About is about the work and the pledge rather than about the
artist, and a portrait leading it would announce a different page from the one
that follows — a biography, which this is not. At the end it is what it
actually is: who wrote that. The onward links come after it, so the last thing
in the column is the way out rather than a picture.

sec-portrait/para4.en:
It is small for the same reason: 9 rem in the homepage section and 10.5 rem on
the page, capped at the column's own width on a phone. A signature, not a
plate. The About page could not have given it a column beside the text in any
case — that page's mount is 660 px around a 34 rem measure, because finding
D-01 brought it in to the column, and 660 less the 544 px the measure takes
leaves 116 px, which is a margin.

sec-portrait/para5.en:
**It is mounted as a painting.** The same cream mat, the same board grain, the
same mount shadow, from the same rule: the stylesheet names `.portrait__img`
alongside `.work__img`, so there is one mat on this site rather than two, and
the artist's photograph is an object on a wall like everything else on it.
What it does not take is everything that would make it a work — no zoom
cursor, no lightbox, no view transition, no entry in the catalogue, no price.
The caption under it is the artist's name, in the small caps a tombstone uses,
in `--muted` at 4.62:1 on the wall; the About page sets its prose in the
display face, and the caption keeps the interface face in both places, because
a signature is not running text.

sec-portrait/para6.en:
**While there is no photograph** the frame holds the image pipeline's own
placeholder card, so the layout is real and can be judged at every width, and
a release build leaves the frame out altogether rather than ship an empty mat.
That is the arrangement rule WK-10 already uses for a work's unshot views, and
it is what keeps this from becoming a permanent gap in the page: a site with
no portrait is a site with no portrait, not a site with a hole in it.

sec-portrait/para7.en:
Two rules hold the two halves of that. **ID-08** is a warning, not a blocker —
a portrait is editorial, not legal, so nothing here can keep the site from
going live — and it reports, in every readiness report, that the frame will be
omitted. **ID-07** is a blocker that cannot be waived, and applies the moment
the photograph is real: a photograph on a page has to be described (1.1.1), and
nobody can describe one that has not been taken, so until then the rule *owns*
`site.about.portrait.alt` and the general placeholder backstop leaves it alone.
Supplying `masters/portrait.jpg` and running the image build is the whole of
turning the frame on; the photograph keeps its own proportions, because the
frame is built from the size the pipeline recorded.

sec-portrait/para8.en:
Four assertions, M-01: that both places sign off with the frame, in both
languages, after the prose and before the links; that it is matted like a
painting, carries its own width and height so it costs no layout shift, and is
in no way a work; that an empty frame is marked as a placeholder and is gated
out of a release; and that the description rule is unwaivable, conditional and
owns its own field.

sec-structure-growth/para1.en:
The depth is fixed at three levels below the homepage — *Works / series / work* —
because more than a few levels is where visitors lose their way;[^nng-flat] growth
is added across, not down.

sec-structure-growth/cell4.en: One entry in `site.json`; page, tab and card follow. Asserted (I-03)

sec-structure-growth/cell5.en: Genres come into use: two or more among available works

sec-structure-growth/cell6.en: A horizontal genre filter row on `/works/`. A genre is a filter, never a fourth level: a landscape in *Tribute* is in one room and matches two filters[^nng-poly]

sec-structure-growth/cell7.en: The Works tabs pass eight, or filter types pass eight

sec-structure-growth/cell8.en: The Works navigation moves to a left column on desktop — the one case the research supports a sidebar. The eight-tab ceiling is asserted today (I-06), so the change cannot happen by accident

sec-structure-growth/cell10.en: The homepage shows six series cards and a link to all

sec-structure-growth/cell11.en: About gains pages — CV, exhibitions, press

sec-structure-growth/cell12.en: About gets its own row of tabs, as Works has

sec-structure-growth/cell14.en: *How to Buy* leaves the header for the footer

sec-structure-held/para1.en:
Assertions I-01 to I-06: the header links to four real pages and marks the
current one; every work is listed exactly once — on *Works*, on its series page, or
among sold works; the homepage shows at most four and states how many there are; a
series needs only data; deeper pages carry a breadcrumb whose last step is the page
itself; the old address still arrives; and no navigation lives in a side column.
The render check covers the catalogue, both series pages and sold works.

sec-structure-held/fn-nng-rail.en: Nielsen Norman Group, [Fight against "right-rail blindness"](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/fight-right-rail-blindness/) and [Banner blindness revisited](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/banner-blindness-old-and-new-findings/).

sec-structure-held/fn-nng-local.en: Nielsen Norman Group, [Local navigation is a valuable orientation and wayfinding aid](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/local-navigation/).

sec-structure-held/fn-baymard-filters.en: Baymard Institute, [Be careful with horizontal filtering toolbars](https://baymard.com/blog/horizontal-filtering-sorting-design).

sec-structure-held/fn-serial.en: The serial-position effect: first and last items in a list are recalled best, the middle worst — Ebbinghaus's finding, summarised for interface work by [Laws of UX](https://lawsofux.com/serial-position-effect/) and applied to navigation order by [CXL](https://cxl.com/blog/serial-position-effect/) and [Convertize](https://tactics.convertize.com/tactic/restructure-your-navigation-menu). Nav orders in @tbl-order were read from each site's rendered header in September 2026.

sec-structure-held/fn-nng-flat.en: Nielsen Norman Group, [Flat vs. deep website hierarchies](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/flat-vs-deep-hierarchy/).

sec-structure-held/fn-nng-poly.en: Nielsen Norman Group, [Polyhierarchies improve findability for ambiguous IA categories](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/polyhierarchy/).

sec-built/para1.en:
Six captures of the preview build, five on a desktop and one on a phone. They
are not mockups: `docs/report/shots.sh` takes them from `dist/` each time this
document is built, so they show the site as it is. The ribbon across the top of
each page and the red `NEEDS-INPUT` flags are the preview's; a release has
neither (@sec-readiness).

sec-built/caption1.en: The homepage as it now stands, with the plates off (@sec-plates): one sage field from the bar to the footer, nothing painted under the content column, and cream kept for the mat around the work — which is what makes the work separate from the ground. Dark brown bar, the SC monogram at the head of the wordmark — the traced vector, in the wordmark's own cream (@sec-mark-vector) — and, at the right, the language switch, which is the one control in the masthead that changes anything (@sec-review-aw). Under the bar, the band, painted in About's darker green: van Gogh's line stands twice, his Dutch from letter 143 to Theo — *wat met liefde gedaan wordt dat wordt goed gedaan* — set small and italic above the reader's own language, with his full name beneath, aligned to the quote's longest line (@sec-band). The featured work follows below it, on a piece of wall of its own proportion with its label at its foot, and each section boundary is stated by an engraved line (@sec-soft-line).

sec-built/caption2.en: A work page. The views of the work — front, detail, edge, back and video — sit in a strip with thumbnails always visible, grey placeholders until the photographs exist. The price is the boldest element in the block. The scale diagram shows the painting against a 244 cm wall and a 213 cm sofa, hung at the museum standard of 144.78 cm, which is also where the mark's datum sits.

sec-built/caption3.en: The sold state. The price stays visible as social proof, "Sold" sits at full contrast in the price position, and the call-to-action slot becomes a capture rather than a dead end.

sec-built/caption4.en: About, set as a book page: the display face at 19.2 px, a lede, a three-line drop cap in sanguine, and the closing quotation in Fraunces' real italic. The mount comes in to 660 px around a 34 rem column, and with its plate transparent it is the shadow and the rim that draw it. At the foot of the prose, the artist's portrait as a sign-off, matted as a painting is and holding the pipeline's placeholder card until the photograph exists (@sec-portrait). The Chinese page is the same page in a system serif, without the drop cap or the italic (@sec-about-type).

sec-built/caption5.en: The homepage on a 390 px phone. The masthead takes two rows — the short name, then the sections and the language switch — and does not stick: a sticky masthead that tall would take a third of the screen and hide the focused item. Van Gogh's line comes before the featured work, and the painting is the full width of its column (@sec-review-aw).

sec-review/para1.en:
The built site was reviewed in September as a designer rather than as its
author. Nineteen findings, in five groups; eighteen were implemented, and each
is held by an assertion of the same number in `check-review.mjs`.

sec-review/tblcap1.en: What the review changed, by group

sec-review/cell6.en: A painting moved into the hero beside the motto; a `mailto:` link stopped calling itself *Buy*; How to Buy gained reachable contact details; the price and its button were bound into one block

sec-review/cell9.en: A footer grey at **2.34:1** — shipped, not theoretical — was removed; the contrast checker was taught to resolve the cascade rather than read declarations; the scale diagram's linework went from 1.73:1 to **3.24:1** and its labels from 3.05:1 to **4.90:1**

sec-review/cell12.en: The icon set, `theme-color` and manifest (@sec-mark); Open Graph typed as a product with price and availability; the sage field restored on a phone

sec-review/cell15.en: Prose pages given a narrower mount; the archive set as a grid rather than a second selling gallery; the gallery name made the `h1`; dead rules deleted

sec-review/cell18.en: The Chinese subset's coverage is now asserted at build time, and each locale preloads only the face it uses

sec-review/para2.en:
Two were not fixes. **C-04** proposed freezing the wordmark in English; it was
declined, and the wordmark still translates. That decision is what later freed
the logo: a monogram is a device beside a name rather than a translation of
one, which is why an `SC` mark can stand beside 常识画廊 (@sec-mark). And half
of **B-03** was wrong: the scale diagram's painting and sofa were said to be
off-axis, and are centred. Its contrast half was real, and is the measurement
above.

sec-review/para3.en:
Re-checked on 18 September against the review as written: all nineteen are
accounted for. Eighteen shipped and every one of them is green in
`check-review.mjs` under its own number; C-04 is recorded there as decided
rather than done. **One part of one finding is still open** — A-02 asked for a
WeChat route for the `zh` locale alongside the enquiry button, and the QR image
that needs does not exist yet. The contact details it depends on are owed too
(@sec-readiness-today), so it is on the list in @sec-content rather than
forgotten.

sec-review-aw/head.en: The second review, against the award

sec-review-aw/para1.en: *Eleven findings, coded `AW-nn`. The document is in `docs/review/`.*

sec-review-aw/para2.en:
The first review asked whether the site was correct. The second asked a
different question — whether a design jury would stop on it — and it was
conducted the same way: the site built, served, and laid out in headless Chrome
at 390, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 px in both locales, with every element box
read out of the DOM rather than estimated from a screenshot. The findings are
in `docs/review/`, with the boxes they were measured from, so a later reader can
re-measure rather than take any of it on trust.

sec-review-aw/para3.en:
Its verdict was that the craft was here and the composition was not, and the
single sentence under that was: **the system was built to hold paintings, and
then configured never to show one at any size.**

sec-review-aw/cell12.en: Latest works on a 390 px phone

sec-review-aw/tblcap1.en: What the second review moved, measured

sec-review-aw/para4.en:
**The wall.** Every painting on the site was held under a constant —
`clamp(260px, 48vh, 460px)` in the hero, 22 rem in the catalogue, 16 rem in the
archive, 14 rem on a series card. A work was therefore the same size on a
27-inch display as on a 13-inch laptop, and *smaller* on a phone than its own
column had offered: a 40 × 30 portrait in a 307 px column wants 409 px, hit the
352 px cap and shrank to 264 wide. A cell is now a piece of **wall**: a box
whose proportion is `--wall-ratio`, the narrowest work in the catalogue, which
`build.js` derives from the data rather than anybody typing it. Every painting
is width-bound and hangs to the bottom-left of its cell, so one left line and
one right line run down the page and the tombstones stay level because the
walls are. A landscape work entering the catalogue widens the wall for
everyone, which is correct: the wall is whatever holds the work.

sec-review-aw/para5.en:
**The opening screen.** It spent its first 556 px on a masthead, a band and a
label, and then showed a painting 12.5% of the screen wide with 65% of its own
block empty beside it. The featured work now stands on a wall of its own
proportion with its label at its foot — the work page's idiom brought forward —
and the tombstone row is back inside the 32 rem the base rule has always capped
it to and always explained.

sec-review-aw/para6.en:
**Three things came out.** The masthead's search, account and cart
(@sec-next-decisions); the band's four decorative rules (@sec-band); and four
`opsz` values pinned to sizes that had become fluid. Each removal is held by
the assertion that had held the thing in place: N-01 holds the ornament *out*
of the band, and H-01 holds the shop bar to its route list in both
directions.

sec-review-aw/para7.en:
**Endings.** A work page closed on a rule and one right-aligned *Next work* —
no route back to the catalogue, nothing from the same series. It closes with
three works now, siblings first and only ones still for sale, and those three
carry their view-transition names, so clicking one flies it out of the grid
into the page it leads to. `check-review` H-05 read "one name per work page",
which is the same thing as the rule that actually matters only while a page
shows one painting; it now asserts that rule — every name distinct, the page's
own exactly once, and never on a detail, an edge, a back or the video.

sec-review-aw/para8.en:
**The share card.** `og:image` pointed at the painting's own file, and a 4:5
canvas under `summary_large_image` is shown as a 1.91:1 sliver of itself
whatever the page declares — while the home page, Works, every series and the
archive declared a 1600 × 1600 square for a 1600 × 2000 file, because only the
work page wrote a height at all. It is drawn rather than cropped now: 1200 ×
630, the sage wall, the painting in its mat, the monogram beside it, one per
work from the same master the pages use. No text on it — text needs a font the
SVG rasteriser can load and CI has no Fraunces, while every platform already
sets `og:title` beside the image. Its colours are read out of `tokens.css`,
like this report's figures, so the card cannot drift from the site it pictures.

sec-review-aw/para9.en:
Building it surfaced a defect older than either review: `og:image` was the one
absolute URL on the page built from a raw path rather than through `path()`, so
on a project site served from `/<repo>/` it lost the prefix that canonical,
`og:url`, hreflang and every sitemap entry kept — and the card 404'd for every
scraper that fetched it.

sec-review-aw/para10.en: Nine of the eleven are closed as written. Two are not.

sec-review-aw/para11.en:
**AW-05 was right about the measurement and wrong about the remedy.** It found
that the flat ground caps the palette — pure black reaches 6.14:1 on the wall,
so running text has 9% of headroom and captions 3% — and proposed painting the
plates, which is what the arithmetic points at. But that corrects the look of
the gallery rather than a defect in it, and @sec-brief is explicit about who
decides those: the ground stays sage. The finding is answered three other ways.
Its bill is printed on every build, so the constraint is never out of sight
(@sec-plates); the alternative is kept one edit away and solved by the same
check (@sec-switch-ground); and the half of the problem it did not address —
that with colour at its ceiling the remaining variable is weight — is
@sec-weight.

sec-review-aw/para12.en:
**AW-10 waits on the shoot.** The prose pages carry no image because there is
no photograph to put on them, and an empty mat on a page that does not need one
yet is worse than white space.

sec-review-look/para1.en:
A last pass over every page type at three widths in both locales, which found
six things that were wrong rather than arguable. They are recorded because each
one had survived the measured reviews: **a measurement finds what you thought to
measure, and looking finds what you did not.**

sec-review-look/item1.en: The **404** still named search, accounts and the cart as the things being built, after the controls that led to it had been withdrawn.

Mainland China is absent from Stripe's\index{Stripe} supported business countries. Hong Kong,
Singapore and Japan are present. This is not the narrower finding about
PayPal — it is the whole account.

the-constraint/para2.en:
Airwallex\index{Airwallex} looked like the answer and is more restricted than it appears. A
mainland entity can open an account for Global Accounts, foreign exchange and
transfers, but card acquiring is excluded in Airwallex's own Chinese-language

sec-individual/head.en: Route A — launch as an individual

sec-individual/para1.en: At this turnover, four obligations that would normally apply do not.

sec-individual/tblcap1.en: What the individual route does not require

sec-individual/cell8.en: **Not consumed** — cross-border e-commerce settles outside it

sec-individual/cell11.en: **Not filed** — resident individuals exempt at or below USD 10,000 per transaction

sec-individual/cell14.en: **Exempt** — monthly sales under CNY 100,000, to 31 Dec 2027

sec-individual/para2.en:
Six works at \$60–\$440 is roughly CNY 19,000 — an order of magnitude below the
registration ceiling.

sec-individual/para3.en:
Route sale proceeds as a gift or family remittance; split transactions to stay
under a threshold; or use informal currency swaps. The last is 私自买卖外汇
under Article 45 of the FX Regulations, and published enforcement puts the
penalty on the offender's PBOC credit file.

sec-hk/head.en: Route B — a Hong Kong sole proprietorship

sec-hk/para1.en:
A Business Registration certificate\index{Hong Kong entity} is sufficient — no incorporation. That
unlocks the free Airwallex plan with no-code payment links, international cards
at 3.60% + HK\$2.35, **and Alipay**\index{Alipay} **and WeChat
Pay**\index{WeChat Pay} as merchant methods, which is how the domestic half of
the audience is served from one checkout.

sec-hk/para2.en:
It also unlocks repatriation: Airwallex supports local CNY transfer for sellers
without a mainland registered business whose ultimate beneficial owner is a
Chinese national exporting goods from the mainland. That describes this business
exactly.

sec-hk/para3.en:
Airwallex approves its Payments product **separately** from account opening, and
reviews the live site as part of that review. The entity list verified covers
account opening only.

rejected/para1.en:
**Payoneer Checkout** is Stripe-powered, excludes mainland China explicitly, and
requires monthly volumes above USD 20,000 — roughly 130× this business.
**PingPong** and **LianLian** both have real independent-site acquiring, but
neither publishes pricing or eligibility and both are sales-led. Do not design
around either without a written quote.

sec-shipping/caption1.en: How each kind of work travels. The paper rule is the one most often got wrong.

sec-shipping/callout1.en: Works on paper ship flat, never rolled

sec-shipping/para1.en:
Rolling cracks the paper's sizing and can crease or smear the media. Tubes are a
fallback for very large **unstretched** canvas only.

sec-shipping/para2.en:
Stretched canvas ships upright, never flat, with the bubble wrap outside the
rigid boards so nothing touches the paint. Cold is a real hazard: linseed oil
stiffens and can crack below freezing, which matters for winter shipping.

sec-shipping/para3.en:
The much-discussed "\$1,000 artwork cap" does not bind here. FedEx caps declared value on art at \$1,000 or \$9.07/lb,
whichever is greater; USPS additional insurance for artwork caps around \$1,000.
Every one of those caps sits above this entire inventory.

sec-duty/head.en: Duty and tax at the border

sec-duty/callout1.en: The site cannot say ``duty-free'' to US buyers

sec-duty/para1.en:
Original paintings under HS 9701\index{HS heading 9701} carry a **Free** base
rate, which is where the belief comes from. For a **China-origin** shipment in
2026 it is wrong.

sec-duty/item1.en: **Section 301 List 4A applies.**\index{Section 301} HTSUS 9903.88.15 imposes **+7.5%** on products of China, and US note 20(s)(i) enumerates `9701.91.00` — contemporary paintings — among the covered subheadings. The exclusion that once covered paintings is expired.

sec-duty/item2.en: **De minimis is suspended.**\index{de minimis} The \$800 exemption no longer applies, so every painting needs a customs entry.

sec-duty/item3.en: **The IEEPA tariffs are gone** — struck down and revoked in February 2026 — and artworks were separately carved out of them as "informational materials". That relief does **not** extend to Section 301.

sec-duty/caption1.en: What a US buyer actually pays on a \$300 painting.

sec-duty/cell15.en: Reduced art rate per member state

sec-duty/caption2.en: The How to Buy page, which puts the duty figure in front of the buyer before they commit rather than after.

sec-donation/para1.en:
The draft said "10% of each order goes toward research", which is a
per-transaction consumer promise. The site now says *"I personally donate 10% of
my profits each quarter"* — a personal pledge, which is a materially different
representation.

sec-donation/para2.en:
What protects the pledge is not the wording but the receipts: a public page with
the recipient named, the basis stated, the cadence disclosed, and a running
cumulative total.

sec-returns/callout1.en: Returns cannot be refused, in either market
sec-returns/callout1.zh: 两个市场都不能拒绝退货

sec-returns/para1.en:
**China.** Consumer Protection Law Art. 25 gives a seven-day no-reason return on
distance sales. The exceptions are a **closed list** — SAIC Order 90 Art. 6
excludes only goods made to the consumer's order, perishables, unsealed digital
media and delivered periodicals. The 2024 Implementing Regulations Art. 19 then
expressly forbid a trader expanding that list, and ban pre-ticked exclusion.
sec-returns/para1.zh: **中国。**《消费者权益保护法》第二十五条规定，远程销售的商品享有七日无理由退货。例外情形是一份**封闭清单**：原国家工商总局第90号令第六条只排除消费者定作的商品、鲜活易腐商品、已拆封的数字化商品，以及已交付的报纸期刊。2024年施行的《实施条例》第十九条进一步明确禁止经营者扩大这份清单，也禁止用默认勾选的方式排除退货。

sec-returns/para2.en:
**European Union.** CRD\index{Consumer Rights Directive} Art. 16(c) excepts goods "made to the consumer's
specifications or clearly personalised". **Uniqueness is not personalisation** —
the test is whether the *buyer* specified it. A pre-existing painting chosen
from a catalogue fails that test.
sec-returns/para2.zh: **欧盟。**《消费者权益指令》\index{Consumer Rights Directive}第16条(c)项对“按消费者要求制作或明显个性化”的商品作出例外规定。**独一无二不等于个性化**——判断标准是这件商品是否由*买家*指定。从作品目录中选购的既有画作不符合这一标准。

sec-returns/para3.en:
A "governed by PRC law" clause does not help: Rome I\index{Rome I Regulation} Art. 6(2) prevents a choice
of law from depriving a consumer of protections that cannot be derogated from
under their home law, where the trader directs activity there. Offering EU
shipping at checkout is directing activity.
sec-returns/para3.zh: 写一条“适用中华人民共和国法律”的条款没有用：根据《罗马条例 I》\index{Rome I Regulation}第6条第2款，经营者在消费者所在国开展经营活动时，法律选择不能剥夺消费者依其本国法律享有、且不得通过约定排除的保护。在结账时提供欧盟配送，就是在当地开展经营活动。

sec-returns/para4.en:
**One worldwide 14-day policy**\index{returns} over-satisfies the Chinese seven days, removes
any need to geo-detect buyers, and avoids a seven-day policy reading as an
attempt to shorten the EU right. Commissions are the one genuine exception under
both regimes.
sec-returns/para4.zh: **全球统一的14天退货政策**\index{returns}既超出中国规定的七天，也不需要识别买家所在地区，还能避免七天的政策被看作是在缩短欧盟法律赋予的权利。在两种法律制度下，委托创作的作品都是唯一真正的例外。

sec-disclosure/para1.en:
One block of address, phone and email satisfies three regimes at once: the EU
Consumer Rights Directive Art. 6(1)(c), the Chinese requirement, and the UK
anticipatory duty. Alongside it, SAMR Order 37 Art. 12 prescribes the exact
sentence an unregistered individual seller must publish:

sec-disclosure/quote1.en: 个人从事零星小额交易活动，依法不需要办理市场主体登记

sec-disclosure/para2.en: That string is quoted verbatim from the rule and must not be paraphrased.

sec-privacy/para1.en:
PIPL\index{PIPL} applies, and costs a privacy page and a one-page impact
assessment — no more. Processing necessary to conclude and perform the sale
needs **no consent checkbox** — a
just-in-time notice at the email field is the correct pattern, and consent is
reserved for the newsletter. No PRC representative and no regulator filing are
required, because those provisions bind handlers *outside* China. The overseas
hosting is exempt from the CAC transfer mechanisms both as contract-necessary
and on volume.

the-legal-position/para1.en:
Calmer than the compliance industry suggests. A one-person operation is almost
certainly exempt from the European Accessibility Act as a microenterprise
providing services. The stronger argument for the work is commercial:
**a blind collector who cannot read the descriptions cannot buy the painting.**

sec-alt/para1.en:
The "125-character limit" is folklore — there is none in the HTML specification
or in WCAG. The citable number is Cooper Hewitt's **approximately fifteen
words**.

sec-alt/para2.en:
The guidance genuinely disagrees on interpretation: the DIAGRAM Center says
never interpret, Cooper Hewitt says interpret when it aids visual understanding.
For an artist's own gallery Cooper Hewitt is right — but interpretation stays
textually separable, labelled "Artist's note", placed last, and never allowed to
replace observation.

sec-alt/para3.en:
Acceptable as a first pass, never as shipped text. A model can report palette,
format and apparent handling. It cannot know the true medium, the real
dimensions, the title, or the intent — which is exactly what a buyer needs. A
wrong description is worse than none, because it burns trust in the channel.

shape/para1.en:
Plain Node, no framework. Thirty-six pages generated from three data files,
with **one npm dependency** — `sharp`, and only for turning photographs into
web derivatives — which is the only architecture consistent with a design whose
argument is restraint. Generating the pages needs Node and nothing else.

shape/para2.en:
Three other things in this repository do need Python, and say so rather than
pretending otherwise: the icon build, the image tool (@sec-image-tool) and this
document. All three want Pillow; the report also wants matplotlib, fontTools
and CairoSVG, and the image tool's trace mode wants VTracer. None of them is
needed to build or check the site, with one exception noted in @sec-checks.

shape/para3.en:
The page count follows the data: eighteen pages per locale for six works in two
series, of which six are work pages.

sec-fingerprints/head.en: The code assets carry their own hash

sec-fingerprints/para2.en:
A page and its stylesheet are two requests, cached separately, and each host
decides for how long. GitHub Pages — the preview target — sends `max-age=600`
on both and does not read `_headers`. So for ten minutes after a deploy a
returning visitor can be handed the previous `/styles.css` with the current
`/index.html`: not a stale site but a **wrong** one, whose two halves disagree
in a way that looks exactly like a change that failed to ship. It was read as
one on 20 September 2026.

sec-fingerprints/para3.en:
The three code assets — the stylesheet and the two scripts — are therefore
written before any page, under names that contain a hash of their own bytes
(`styles.cd55845f.css`), and each page names the files it was built against. A
name that contains the bytes cannot be served for other bytes: old page with
old stylesheet, together, until the page expires; new page with new stylesheet,
at once. Nothing here shortens the ten minutes — no file in this repository can,
on a host that ignores `_headers` — but whatever a visitor is holding is
internally consistent. On Cloudflare Pages, which does read `_headers`, the
same names earn the three of them a year, `immutable`.

sec-fingerprints/para4.en: Three assertions hold it, and the third is the one worth reading:

sec-fingerprints/item1.en: every reference on every built page carries a hash, each resolves to a file, and **no plain-named copy is left in `dist/`** for a stale page to find;

sec-fingerprints/item2.en: the hashed names are frozen for a year and `availability.json` is still 60 seconds — the one file at the root that must not be frozen, because it is how a page finds out it has sold;

sec-fingerprints/item3.en: `availability.js` works out the deployment base by stripping its own filename off its own `src`, so that one file serves a domain root and a Pages subpath. The hash broke that expression. The base became the whole script URL, the sold check fetched `/availability.<hash>.jsavailability.json`, and the 404 landed in the `catch` that is there for being offline — so every sold work would have gone on showing as for sale, with nothing in the console to say so. The expression is now solved in the check against the name the build actually writes, at a root and under a base path.

sec-fingerprints/para5.en:
Which is the general lesson, and it is cheap to state: content-addressing a
file changes its name, and **everything that parses that name is part of the
change** — here, the sold check, `check-review.mjs`, which finds the stylesheet
in order to read it, and `preview.mjs`, which inlines it into a single-file
review copy. Each of them now takes the name from the page rather than assuming
it.

sec-image-tool/head.en: Converting between a drawing and pixels

sec-image-tool/para1.en:
`scripts/image.py` (`npm run image`) is the one place the project converts
between the two, in both directions, and it states what each conversion costs
instead of choosing quietly:

sec-image-tool/cell4.en: True vector geometry — every decoded pixel as an integer-aligned rectangle, horizontal runs merged. No quantization, smoothing, denoising, recolouring or resampling, and no compression either: large, and exact

sec-image-tool/cell6.en: The original file, byte for byte, inside an SVG `<image>`. Visually lossless and honest about being a raster in a vector wrapper

sec-image-tool/cell8.en: VTracer infers regions and paths. Compact, and an **approximation** — which is what `--verify` is for

sec-image-tool/cell10.en: SVG or SVGZ back to a raster at a stated size, optionally flattened onto a colour, because alpha is the commonest thing to lose by accident

sec-image-tool/para2.en:
The output format is chosen by the **extension**, so the name of a file and its
contents cannot disagree: `.svg` `.svgz` `.pdf` `.ps` `.eps` on the vector side,
`.png` `.webp` `.jpg` `.tif` on the raster side. The geometry is always built as
SVG; PDF, PS and EPS are that SVG handed to Cairo, which is a container change
and not a second approximation. Two things follow and are said rather than
discovered: the `<metadata>` audit block only survives in the SVG containers,
because PDF and PostScript have nowhere to keep it, and a pixel-mode page of a
million rectangles is a million rectangles in PDF too — for print, `trace` or
`embed` is almost always what is wanted. A format that cannot carry alpha, such
as JPEG, refuses an image that has some until `--on` says what it should sit on.

sec-image-tool/para3.en:
The input file is never written to, and every output carries a `<metadata>`
block naming its source, that source's SHA-256 and the mode, so a derived file
can always be traced back. `--verify` renders the result back at native size
and reports per-channel error, composited over black and over white as well as
raw, because a renderer may legitimately rewrite RGB wherever alpha is low.

sec-image-tool/para4.en:
It has a `selftest`, and `npm run check` runs it: two fixtures — flat runs,
a single pixel against a run, and partial alpha — both directions, requiring
byte-exactness when the source is opaque and one unit per channel when it is
not. A tool nobody re-tests is a tool that quietly stops working before the
day somebody needs it.

sec-switch/para1.en:
One string in `seller.json` moves the whole site between the two commercial
routes:

sec-switch/para2.en:
That switches the published legal disclosure, the invoicing language, the
checkout provider and the returns basis together. No template knows which entity
is active.

sec-oversell/caption1.en: Defence in depth. Each layer above the bottom one fails in a way the bottom one survives.

sec-oversell/para1.en:
No platform in this price range guarantees atomicity. The client-side
availability check is roughly forty lines and is the only layer that survives a
stale CDN page, a silently failed rebuild or a bfcache restore.

sec-oversell/para2.en:
Alongside it, a published policy costs nothing and settles the residual case:
*in the rare event two people buy the same piece at once, the first completed
payment stands and the second is refunded in full within 24 hours.*

sec-checks/para1.en:
`npm run check` runs the first four in seconds. The rendering check needs
Chrome; GitHub runs it on every preview, and the release runs all of them.

sec-checks/para2.en:
One of the four reaches outside Node: `check-review` ends by running the image
tool's own selftest, which is Python. That was a deliberate choice over letting
it skip when Python is bare — a check that can quietly not run is not a check —
and the CI workflow installs the four wheels it needs so that it always does.

sec-checks/cell4.en: Any token below its floor on the darkest ground it is painted on — resolving the cascade, so the declaration that actually wins is the one measured — and the glass bar under 7:1 over white. With the plates off it also prints, without blocking, every pair as the page actually renders it (@sec-plates)

sec-checks/cell6.en: A dead link; missing `alt`, `width` or `height`; heading order; landmarks; hreflang; a Chinese character the font subset does not cover; a placeholder route that resolves. In a release, any `NEEDS-INPUT` or placeholder at all

sec-checks/cell8.en: **99 assertions over 62 findings** — both design reviews, the mark, softness, the header and the views, the structure, the flags and the gate — written against the built pages, so a fix that stops being applied fails the build

sec-checks/cell10.en: Any of **48 tests** showing the gate opens only when it should (@sec-readiness-proof)

sec-checks/cell12.en: The image tool failing its own round-trip: two fixtures, both directions, byte-exact when the source is opaque and within one unit per channel when it is not (@sec-image-tool)

sec-checks/cell14.en: In Chrome, at 1440, 900, 390, 360 and 320 px across 12 pages: a painting out of its own proportions, rounded or transformed; a masthead that overflows, takes more than two rows or has a control under 44 px; either half of van Gogh's line re-wrapped, its attribution off the quote's edge, or the featured work ahead of the quote

sec-checks/para3.en:
Headless Chrome will not lay a page out narrower than 500 px — asked for 390, it
lays out at 500 and crops. Phone widths are therefore laid out inside an iframe
of exactly that width, with scrollbars hidden, and the check asserts the width
the page actually received.

sec-checks/callout1.en: A test that passes for the wrong reason

sec-checks/para4.en:
One of the review fixes set `font-size:var(--size-h1)`. No such token exists —
the scale calls it `--size-hero` — so the rule silently fell back to inherited
body size, and the assertion written for it passed because it only matched the
declaration's text. The repair was a cross-cutting assertion that every
`var(--token)` in the shipped stylesheet resolves to a definition. An
undefined custom property is the one CSS error that produces no error.

sec-checks/para5.en:
Automated testing decides roughly 13–30% of WCAG success criteria and catches
almost none of the focus-order and focus-visibility failures that block people
outright. The checks are a floor, not a pass.

sec-checks-comment/para1.en:
Worth recording, because it is the kind of failure a suite of 98 assertions
can walk straight past. A comment in `tokens.css` had been closed twice: the
second terminator ended it early, and everything after it — up to and
including the declaration of `--sanguine` — was parsed as garbage and dropped
by the browser. The site ran for a day without its accent colour: no
terracotta focus ring, no filled button hover.

sec-checks-comment/para2.en:
Nothing caught it. The token check greps the stylesheet's TEXT for the
declaration, and the text was there. The contrast gate strips comments
non-greedily before reading the tokens, and found it too. Every figure in this
document that reads `tokens.css` read it the same way. Only a browser knew,
and a browser is what found it: a decorative rule in the new band would not
paint.

sec-checks-comment/para3.en:
The assertion that would have caught it now exists — after stripping comments
from each stylesheet, no orphan terminator may remain, and every declaration
the raw file makes must still be present in what the parser would see. It is
the cheapest kind of check and it holds a whole class of silent loss.

sec-readiness/para1.en:
The site must not go live until every critical detail is supplied. A list of
fields marked `NEEDS-INPUT` is not enough to ensure that: an empty email,
`test@example.com` or a placeholder photograph contains no such word, and a list
that is printed does not stop a build that is published. The readiness gate
checks what is in each field, and a release cannot be built while it is closed.

sec-readiness-research/item1.en: **Fail closed.** When a control cannot establish that it is safe to proceed, it should stop rather than carry on — the security principle usually called *failing securely*.[^owasp-fail] For this site the unsafe state is a shop that looks open and is not lawful or not honest.

sec-readiness-research/item2.en: **The law names what is critical.** For distance sales to EU consumers, the trader's identity, geographical address, telephone number and email, the main characteristics of the goods, the total price and the arrangements for payment must all be given.[^crd] China's E-Commerce Law requires the business licence information — or the statement that registration is not required — to be shown continuously in a prominent place on the homepage.[^ecl15]

sec-readiness-research/item3.en: **Validate values, not words.** A real email address is best checked against the definition every browser uses, a deliberate, practical subset of RFC 5322.[^whatwg] Some names are reserved precisely so they can never be real — `example.com`, `.test`, `.invalid`[^rfc2606] — which makes an address on one an example nobody replaced. A telephone number in international form has a country code and at most fifteen digits.[^e164] A WeChat ID is six to twenty letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, beginning with a letter.[^wechat]

sec-readiness-research/item4.en: **Gates must be visible.** A documented case from this month: a Cloudflare Pages production build failed, the previous version kept being served, and every check on the repository stayed green, so nobody knew.[^cf-silent] A gate on the host alone is necessary and not sufficient.

sec-readiness-design/item1.en: **A rules engine over the data** (`scripts/readiness.mjs`): 28 rules, each with an area, a severity, the condition under which it applies, the fix, and the law or finding it rests on. It reads nothing and writes nothing, so the build, the report and the tests ask the same question.

sec-readiness-design/item2.en: **Values, with the word as backstop.** Every critical field has a rule that checks what is in it; a final rule catches `NEEDS-INPUT`, *TODO*, *lorem ipsum* and the like anywhere no specific rule reaches, and reports only what no other rule already has.

sec-readiness-design/item3.en: **Conditions.** Hong Kong registration numbers apply only while that entity is active; the transaction ceiling only once the cart takes payments; a donation recipient only while the pledge is above zero. A conditional rule *owns* its fields, so the backstop cannot block on a field its rule has deliberately set aside.

sec-readiness-design/item4.en: **Undecided is not declined.** An optional channel is either a handle or `""`, which removes it from the site. Left as `NEEDS-INPUT` it is undecided, and blocks.

sec-readiness-design/item5.en: **Preview by default; release by request.** Any build not explicitly a release is a preview: noindex on every page, a ribbon saying it is not open for sales and how many details are owed, and — while anything is owed — purchase controls that are drawn but cannot be used. A release asks the gate before building and again inside the build, which refuses *before* clearing the previous output.

sec-readiness-design/item6.en: **Nothing of the preview survives a release.** In release mode the link check fails on a single `NEEDS-INPUT` anywhere — attributes and structured data included — on any placeholder photograph, video or asset, on the ribbon, and on any unusable button. Views without photographs are left out rather than shown.

sec-readiness-design/item7.en: **Waivers with an expiry.** A blocker that can wait may be waived with a reason, a name and a date; expired or unsigned waivers do not count, and every live one is printed in every report and written into the release. Identity, the registration disclosure, returns, prices, dimensions, photographs and payment links cannot be waived — a waiver naming one keeps the gate shut. That includes the Chinese registration declaration, which must match the rule's wording character for character (rule LG-01).

sec-readiness-design/item8.en: **Loud where it matters.** The production host's build command is the release script, so a closed gate is never published; a *Release check* workflow runs the same script on GitHub and fails red with the report on the run's summary page, and the preview workflow shows the report on every run.

sec-readiness-proof/item1.en: **The gate opens when it should.** A copy of the data with every critical detail supplied passes; 32 single breakages each close it on the named rule; five waiver cases — valid, expired, unsigned, scoped to another field, and aimed at a rule that cannot be waived — each behave as specified. 48 tests, in `npm run check`; weakening the 14-day rule or the reserved-domain list turns them red.

sec-readiness-proof/item2.en: **End to end, on completed data.** With the fields temporarily supplied and the three header placeholders of the time waived, the release ran: 0 blockers, 36 pages, no `NEEDS-INPUT` anywhere, no ribbon, all 40 purchase controls live, views without photographs omitted, the three waivers written into `readiness.json`, and every check green in release mode. Saatchi's is the closest model for a painter: it is the only one whose
thumbnails answer the question a buyer of a unique object actually has — *what
will this look like on my wall?*

sec-next-research/para1.en:
**Thumbnails, always.** Every desktop site in Baymard's benchmark shows
thumbnails for additional images; 76% of mobile sites do not. Where only dot
indicators are shown, half of desktop test users had difficulty finding the
additional images, and users missed the one that would have answered their
question. On mobile, a partly visible last thumbnail signals that more
exist.[^baymard-thumbs]

sec-next-research/para2.en:
**At least one image in scale.** 42% of users try to judge a product's size
from its images, and 28% of sites give them nothing to judge by.[^baymard-scale]
For a painting sold unframed, whose size is its single most consequential
property after the image itself, this is the finding that matters most.

sec-next-research/para3.en:
**Different images answer different questions.** Product-page guidance commonly
separates a plain view, an in-scale view, a close-up of material and texture,
and a view in use. For a painting those become: the front, a raking-light
detail, the edge and back, and the work at true size on a wall.

sec-next-research/para4.en:
**No auto-rotation, and real controls.** The W3C pattern for a carousel requires
a stop control whenever slides rotate on their own, stops rotation on focus and
hover, and prefers a tab-style picker when slides are chosen directly — which is
what a thumbnail rail is.[^apg-carousel]

sec-next-research/para5.en:
**Icons need words.** Only the house, the printer and the magnifying glass are
close to universally recognised; everything else — a person, a bag, a heart —
is ambiguous without a visible label, and a label shown only on hover does not
exist on a phone.[^nng-icons]

sec-next-research/para6.en:
**Search should be as prominent as search is useful.** Where people browse
visually — Baymard's examples are apparel and home décor, and art is the same
kind of purchase — a small search control is right; dominant search fields
belong to large catalogues bought by specification.[^baymard-search]

sec-next-research/para7.en:
**Urgency must be true.** EU law treats falsely claiming limited availability to
rush a decision as unfair in all circumstances.[^ucpd] A unique work *is*
available once, so a scarcity bar would not be false here — but the page
already says *Unique work*, and a "Hurry" is pressure the brief rules out.

sec-next-constraints/para1.en:
A shop template assumes multiple units of many products, an account system and
one checkout for everything in the cart. None of those is true of this site yet.

sec-next-constraints/item1.en: **Every work is unique.** A quantity stepper has one legal value. "Only 1 left" is permanently true.

sec-next-constraints/item2.en: **The catalogue is small.** Search earns its place only by finding what a visitor would actually type — a title, a medium, a year, a series — in either language, and nothing else.

sec-next-constraints/item3.en: **There is no server.** The site is static by design. Accounts need authentication, password recovery and storage of personal data — which makes Priscilla a data controller under both PIPL and GDPR (@sec-privacy) for nothing the buying path requires. The payment provider already holds the buyer's record.

sec-next-constraints/item4.en: **There is no multi-item checkout yet.** On the launch route each work has its own payment link, or is sold by enquiry. Whether a provider on either route can take several works in one hosted checkout is **not established** (@tbl-open).

sec-next-constraints/item5.en: **A cart widens the overselling window.** @sec-oversell defends a unique work from being sold twice. A cart invites a buyer to believe a work is held while it sits there, and every layer of that defence has to re-check it.

sec-next-built/item2.en: **Icons only, at every width.** The research above favours visible words; the reference Priscilla chose shows icons alone, and that is what was built — only the magnifying glass is close to universal. sec-next-built/item3.en: **A bilingual 404.** Every placeholder lands on it: both languages, no canonical, not indexed, not in the sitemap. What arrives there is a mistyped address, an old link, or a footer channel mark whose handle is owed, so it names no feature in particular.

sec-next-built/item4.en: **The five views.** Front, detail, edge, back and video on every work page, in a scroll-snap strip that swipes natively, with thumbnails always visible — a rail from 900 px, a row below that. It works with no script. A small script adds what links cannot: the current thumbnail marked for screen readers, no history entry per thumbnail, arrow keys, Home and End, and a video that pauses when it leaves the strip. sec-next-built/item5.en: **Placeholders that step aside.** The image pipeline draws a labelled placeholder for each missing view at a sensible proportion; a real photograph replaces it on the next build and keeps its own proportions. appendix-sources-and-method-/para1.en:
**Colour.** Ratios computed with the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula. The
draft's values were extracted from the PDF content stream rather than sampled
from a render, so they are declared values. Figures in this document read the
project's live token file.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para2.en:
**Fonts.** Built with fonttools 4.59.1 from the variable originals; byte counts
are measured output, not estimates.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para3.en:
**Reachability from mainland China.** Measured against a GFW measurement
service, with known-blocked controls validating the method before any result was
accepted.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para4.en:
**Regulatory material.** Chinese provisions read from `gov.cn` and
`safe.gov.cn`; EU instruments from the Publications Office; US tariff treatment
from the HTSUS and the Federal Register. Article numbers are given so each can
be checked.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para5.en:
**Layout.** Verified in headless Chrome at 1440, 900, 390, 360 and 320 px, not
by description; phone widths are laid out in an iframe of the stated width,
because Chrome will not lay a window out below 500 px (@sec-checks). The
captures in @sec-built are taken from `dist/` by `docs/report/shots.sh` as part
of this document's build, so they cannot show a version of the site that is no
longer shipping.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para6.en:
**If this is printed.** It is meant to be, so the things a printer asks for
are settled rather than left to them.

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell2.en: **A4, 210 × 297 mm.** Set in `preamble.tex`, not in the front matter — Quarto passes neither `papersize` nor its `geometry` list to this template, and the document was US Letter for its whole life while every margin in it was given in millimetres. Found by measuring the PDF

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell4.en: The sage band and the page canvas both run off the edge, so trim-size artwork is not enough. `npm run report:print` writes a second file, `…-print.pdf`: 230 × 317 mm, the A4 trim centred in it, the edge artwork carried **3 mm** past the knife, and crop marks 3 mm outside the trim and 4 mm long

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell6.en: All embedded and subset — Inter, Fraunces, Noto Serif SC and the Latin Modern the maths uses

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell8.en: **RGB.** Ask the press to convert with a stated profile rather than converting it here blind; the palette is warm brown, sage and cream, which separates without drama

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell10.en: Every figure is **285 ppi or better** at its placed size, except three, all deliberate: the prototype sheet at 247, the lockup plate at 210 and the variations panel at 273 — all three are supply-limited (@sec-mark-issues, open item 7) — and the small tiles inside @fig-mark-sizes and @fig-mark-construction at 91, which are 16 px and 32 px renderings shown enlarged, where the pixels *are* the subject

appendix-sources-and-method-/cell12.en: The page is tinted edge to edge. For a long run on a press that charges by coverage, `\canvaspaperfalse` in `preamble.tex` gives white pages and keeps the sage band

appendix-sources-and-method-/para7.en:
**A cross-reference that became a footnote number.** Every `@sec-plates` in
this document rendered as *1* for one build: a line inside a bullet list began
`(@sec-plates) the ground beneath…`, and in Pandoc a line that starts with
`(@label)` followed by a space is an **example-list item**, not a reference. It
defined an example called `sec-plates`, and from then on every reference to
that label resolved to the example's number instead of the section. Nothing
warned: the label was valid, the section was numbered, and the output was a
plausible-looking numeral. Keep a parenthesised reference off the start of a
line, or follow it with punctuation rather than a space.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para8.en:
**The paper.** This document's pages are the site's own reading surface,
`--wash-pale`, flat. They carried the site's canvas tile until 20 September
2026; the site's reading surfaces are untextured now, so this one is too
(@sec-soft-canvas). One 300 dpi image has left the underside of every page

appendix-sources-and-method-/para9.en:
**Figure quality.** Page captures are taken at 2×, resampled to 1772 px — 287 dpi
where they are placed — and kept **lossless**: a screenshot is type and UI edges,
and since the site acquired a texture a JPEG artefact in a capture of it cannot
be told apart from the texture itself. The photographic plates — the prototype
sheet, the lockup, the variations panel and the page canvas — are JPEG at
quality 95 with no chroma subsampling, which is the right codec for continuous
tone and visually lossless at this size.

appendix-sources-and-method-/para10.en:
**The mark.** @fig-brand and @fig-mark are `brand/brand-sheet.png` and
`brand/mark-lockup.png` reproduced as supplied, and the mark in this document's
footer is the same crop of the lockup that the browser tab gets — the report
imports the icon build's own cropping rule rather than repeating it, so the
document, the tab and the masthead cannot be three different drawings. Both
originals are pinned by hash (@sec-mark-sheet).
